News.title: Women will be killed as a result of Government’s ‘unsafe’ early release scheme, probation bosses warns
News.content:
PROBATION bosses are warning women will be killed because of the ­Government’s “unsafe” early release scheme, The Sun on Sunday can reveal.

The union Napo, which ­represents probation and court staff, has also declared no ­confidence in the Prison and Probation Service.



Bosses are now balloting on strike action after slamming PM Andy Burnham and Justice Secretary Alex Norris in a message to members.

Mr Burnham has been forced to roll back parts of the “unfit” release programme after a public backlash.



Serious sex offenders including rapists will now be excluded from the plan.

But there will be no change to manslaughter cases — meaning two of the killers of PC Andrew Harper’s killers are due out.



Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole will be eligible to leave prison after serving half their sentences.

A petition against the thugs’ early release has passed 810,000 signatures.

In total, from next month the number of offenders monitored by tags, which are overseen by ­probation workers, will hit 40,000 — up from 28,000 earlier this year.

Ministers are now said to be looking at further U-turns in the first major scandal of Mr Burnham’s premiership.



Napo says the reversals do not go far enough, warning in a major intervention that ministers have failed to “address the real issues of public and safe releases”.

The union wrote to members: “The Prime Minister and the Justice Secretary have failed to ­acknowledge the probation workloads crisis that has afflicted the service for over two years.”

A senior union source said “plans to release thousands of domestic abuse perpetrators and stalkers early” mean “more people, largely women, will be killed or harmed”.

Ian Lawrence, Napo’s General Secretary, told The Sun on Sunday: “Everyone is talking about prisons, and yes it is bad, but the crisis in probation is far worse. But yet again, our members are being overlooked while all the attention is on prison.”

Shadow safeguarding minister Alicia Kearns told The Sun on Sunday: “Probation officers are the last line of defence between dangerous men and the women they target. When they warn Labour’s early release scheme will get women murdered, every minister should be shamed into acting to protect us. Scrap this scheme now.”



The Ministry of Justice said “Our record £700million investment in probation and community punishment is ensuring staff have the resources and powers to manage offenders safely in the community.”

News.title: Andy Burnham suggested FORCING  private landlords to sell rental homes just months before becoming PM
News.content:
ANDY Burnham suggested private landlords should be forced to sell their rental homes just months before becoming PM.

He called for more “public control” of housing so that properties could be made energy-efficient “quickly” to meet green targets.



Speaking at an eco-summit in March when he was Mayor of Greater Manchester, Mr Burnham said: “We can, if necessary, take homes out of the private rented sector and put them into the public housing stock so that we can give people homes that are cheaper to rent and cheaper to run.”

Shadow energy minister Andrew Bowie said: “Under the guise of Net Zero, Andy Burnham wants to send officers of the state to your door and take your home.



“We should just make electricity cheap and let people choose what works for them, rather than threatening repossession.”

Sources said Mr Burnham was specifically talking about Manchester and that his ideas at the time are not government policy.

Under Mr Burnham, Greater Manchester set a target of carbon neutrality by 2038 which includes steps to improve homes.

He also previously called for private rental properties that do not meet legal requirements in the Decent Homes Standard to be bought by councils through compulsory purchase orders.

News.title: Six seriously injured after passenger and freight train collide as local helped rescue trapped travellers using forklift
News.content:
SIX people have been seriously injured after two trains collided in a horror crash.

A freight train and a passenger train smashed into each other between Sveti Ivan Žabno and Gradec stations in Croatia.



The Ministry of Health said six passengers suffered serious injuries, while a further 13 people are believed to have been left with minor injuries.

Emergency services rushed to the scene shortly after 10am, treating the injured before taking them to hospitals in Bjelovar and Koprivnica.



Some of the casualties were later transferred to hospitals in Zagreb.

The most seriously injured is a young woman who is currently in intensive care, but remains in a stable condition.



There were 27 passengers aboard the passenger train when the collision happened.

All those caught up in the horror crash have since been pulled from the wreckage.



Koprivnica-Križevci County Prefect Tomislav Golubić praised emergency crews for their rapid response.

“I must give special thanks to the fire departments in Križevci and Đurđevac, as well as all the volunteer firefighters from the Sveti Ivan area who contributed 50 firefighters to the rescue effort,” he said.

“I would especially like to thank a local man for arriving first at the scene with his personal forklift, making it easier for emergency services to tend to the injured.”

Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Croatian Veterans Tomo Medved later arrived at the scene and also thanked emergency services for their rapid response.

The cause of the crash remains unclear.



Preliminary information suggests a technical failure or human error could have caused the two trains to collide, Medved said.

An investigation is now underway to establish exactly what happened.

Križevci is a city in Koprivnica-Križevci County, in northwestern Croatia.

This comes only days after a train smashed into a hay-filled trailer after an intoxicated farmer stopped on a level crossing.

Astonishing footage showed bales of hay thrown into the air as the train collides with the trailer at high speed.



The incident occurred around midday on August 3 at a railway crossing in Tczew County, in the north of Poland.

It is understood 500 people were on the train at the time of the crash.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

One passenger said: “I was sitting in the first carriage, and the impact was felt strongly.”

Local media reported the driver, a 67- year-old man, is likely to face criminal charges.

News.title: Professor Arday case proves just how much ruling class are in thrall to DEI… it’s time we dumped this toxic ideology
News.content:
JUST for a moment, imagine someone approached you in the pub this weekend and told you they’d once played football semi-professionally.

Big deal, you’d most likely think.



Anyone who’s ever laced a pair of boots these days claims to have had a trial at some time or other.

Ah, but had any of them simultaneously taken up snooker and won serious cash in tournaments all over London?



Well, that is impressive, I suppose.

Not just that, but this extraordinary-sounding fellow would also claim to have run 30 marathons in 35 days (partly with a broken leg, no less!) — a feat even the most elite long-distance ­runners would struggle to emulate.

On top of that, he just so happened to be a highly decorated scholar at one of the world’s most elite ­universities, ­published multiple times and garlanded by leading academics the world over.

Come off it, you’d think — now you’re being silly. Oh, and to top it all, he grew up disabled and only learned to actually speak when he was 11 years old.

At this point of the conversation, most sane people would politely return to their pint and dismiss their fellow ­tippler as a Walter Mitty figure whose tall tales were possibly lifted from the pages of Boy’s Own.

And yet, incredibly, the supposedly learned dons of Cambridge University swallowed every word this man said — hook, line and sinker.



The fantastical case of Professor Jason Arday will doubtless have provided ­people with much amusement this week.

But beyond the laughs, the fact so many supposedly high-minded individuals were taken in by Arday’s tall tales reveals something rather alarming about the establishment which quietly rule us.

Even the most basic research conducted by the Press in recent weeks revealed gaping inconsistencies in his supposed life story.

Not just his dubious claims of sporting achievement but, more ­importantly, the fact significant parts of his research appear to have been ­plagiarised.



But Cambridge seemingly failed to carry out even the most basic of checks.

Or, at least, they chose not to. It’s impossible to get away from the sense the bigwigs there simply couldn’t wait to announce Arday as the ­University’s youngest ever black professor.

Because the truth is, whether it’s the BBC, the NHS or even the police, our public bodies are nowadays in thrall to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion.

It has become the central religion of the ruling class, so much so that ­credentials play second fiddle to ­identity.



People are now promoted, protected or celebrated not primarily for what they can do, but for what they represent.

Even questioning it can see you branded a pariah.

I’m sorry, but this is deeply unfair.

Even worse, it is incredibly patronising to the very people it claims to help.

It makes me shudder to think how many talented academics were passed over in favour of Arday by those ­desperate to parade their diversity credentials.



Worst of all are the hugely talented academics from minority backgrounds whose entirely bona fide credentials could now be looked upon with ­suspicion because of this man’s duplicity.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Britain became great by valuing excellence, hard work and individual achievement.

I say it’s time we dumped this toxic DEI ideology and got back to ­judging everyone on merit.

News.title: If Andy Burnham failed to spot prisons crisis, how will he cope in massive live emergency?
News.content:
You can’t wing it as PM, Mr Burnham

KEIR STARMER’S former right-hand man Morgan McSweeney admitted the ex-PM and his top team were never ready to govern.

The Number Ten chief of staff for almost two years admitted last month: “We didn’t prepare enough for what kind of world we were going to be in.”



It is a spot-on assessment of Sir Keir’s disastrous Labour regime.

But if that was true of a leader who fought and conclusively won a general election, what does it say about our new unelected Prime Minister Andy Burnham?



First he was anointed unopposed without any proper manifesto or scrutiny.

Then he offered two weeks of glad-handing and feelgood vibes.

Before we knew it he was swanning off on holiday, leaving the country in the midst of a full-blown prisons crisis.

A crisis which, by the way, has been on the horizon for nearly three years.

Instead of preparing for the tough decisions needed to meet this head-on, the new PM made sympathetic noises.

He then feebly held up his hands and said it was impossible to prevent the early release of two of the thugs responsible for the death of hero PC Andrew Harper.



The British people are rightly furious.

This has resulted in a petition with the best part of a million signatures opposing the release of unrepentant yobs Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole.

Only now does it seem likely that Mr Burnham will consider a U-turn to find a way out of the mess he has created for himself.

It won’t be easy. It may involve new legislation. It may even involve some hard work to re-open shuttered prisons like HMP Dartmoor, which is sitting empty but expected to cost taxpayers £100million.

But leadership involves planning as well as tackling difficult and unpopular issues.



Which raises a vital question.

If Andy Burnham failed to spot THIS crisis coming, how will he cope when a massive live emergency is thrown at him?

End tax whipround

OUR story on Pages 14 and 15 about the PIP benefit claimant who also works as a dominatrix raises serious questions.

Melanie Bull claims more than £1,000 a month in welfare, some of which is compensation for being so disabled that her work prospects are limited.

But she can also earn up to £1,000 a month financially humiliating her clients.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The DWP needs to investigate.

Her clients may get their kicks from being financially humiliated. Taxpayers do not.

News.title: Moment stalker, 27, found hiding under bed by armed police after mowing down three people while speeding in car
News.content:
THIS is the moment a stalker who crashed into three people is found hiding under a bed by armed police.

Footage shows the officers shining a torch on Joseph Wicks, 27, and telling him “the game’s up”.



The “aggressive” man from Colchester hit three people after he mounted a kerb on Queen Street on November 30 last year.

He then fled the scene and abandoned the car in Wivenhoe Quay but was tracked down after police found his fingerprints inside the Fiat 500.



During the crash, Wicks narrowly missed other members of the public, drove the wrong way along one-way streets, sped along narrow roads and ignored red traffic lights.

While he was being investigated by Essex Police, Wicks subjected a woman to a campaign of stalking and harassment which ended on May 8 when he allegedly attended the victim’s address.

He shouted, swore, and acted aggressively, banging on the front door and demanding entry.

After returning to his van, a man approached opening the passenger door to speak to Wicks about his behaviour.

He reported seeing a metal baseball bat and what appeared to be a handgun inside.

Wicks left the area but continued to bombard the woman with threatening phone calls and messages.



Officers began hunting for Wicks after the report of a potential firearm and located his van the next day, they found the baseball bat but no handgun.

Two days later they attended another address where several people said they had not seen Wicks.

But when they searched the property they found him hiding underneath a bed frame.

Wicks was arrested and charged with a number of offences including dangerous driving, driving while disqualified, driving without insurance, failing to stop for police, three counts of assault by beating, three counts of attempting to cause actual bodily harm, stalking, possession of an imitation firearm with intent to cause fear of violence, sending threatening communications and criminal damage.

While admitting to many of the charges, he denied having an imitation firearm.



Appearing for sentence at Ipswich Crown Court on Friday, July 31, Wicks, was jailed for four years and six months. He was also disqualified from driving for two years and six months.

Inspector Tom Stokes, of our Force Support Unit, said: “Our officers are trained to deal with some of the most challenging and high-risk situations policing can present.

“Every deployment requires calm judgement, clear decision-making and the ability to assess rapidly changing circumstances while keeping the public, colleagues and themselves safe.

“In this case, officers were tasked with locating and arresting a man linked to a series of serious offences, including dangerous driving which put members of the public at risk and a report involving what was believed to be a firearm.

“When information suggests there may be a weapon involved, we must plan carefully and act decisively.



“The professionalism shown by the officers involved meant they were able to safely enter the address, carry out a thorough search and locate Wicks despite efforts to conceal himself.

“Their actions ensured a high-harm offender was brought before the courts and held accountable for his actions.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Much of the work carried out by armed officers happens out of the public eye, but it is built on extensive training, teamwork and a commitment to protecting communities across Essex.

“We will continue to target those who pose the greatest risk and ensure they are brought to justice.”

News.title: Cheating Scots minister outed by wife in front of packed church service as she reveals affair with parishioner
News.content:
SIN OF A PREACHER MAN Cheating Scots minister outed by wife in front of packed church service as she reveals affair with parishioner

A MINISTER’S wife stunned worshippers at a packed church service by announcing he has been having an affair with a parishioner.

Rev Edward Lyons, 48, is set to face a conduct probe over the accusation by spouse Caroline, 45.



A source in Newton Stewart, Wigtownshire, said: “He preaches thou shalt not commit adultery but might be a total hypocrite.”

The disgraced reverend was seen loading a bike and other belongings into a Volkswagen Touran outside the manse he shared with wife of 22 years Caroline, 45.



Later the motor was parked outside an address understood to be the home of the other woman just minutes away.

Church of Scotland officials say they are looking into claims made by Caroline during a sermon that Rev Lyons had been cheating on her with a parishioner in Newton Stewart, Wigtownshire.

Caroline later took to social media to ask where she could find packing boxes.

Locals said Rev Lyons and the parishioner had been spotted doing a supermarket shop together.

The claims about the “trendy” clergyman, who is a karate blackbelt, have stunned the congregation at Penninghame St John’s Church.

A source told The Scottish Sun on Sunday: “Everybody is talking about it. Edward was very popular and highly thought of so these allegations have come as a complete and utter shock.



“He’s just the stereotypical trendy young minister.

“He has longer hair, a beard, he plays electric guitar, does karate and rides a bike. His wife said he had been cheating on her with a senior member of the flock and it looks like she has booted him out.

“Edward appears to be staying with the new woman and they’ve been seen down at the supermarket. He preaches family values and thou shalt not commit adultery but it seems he might be a total hypocrite.”

Lyons, from Drumchapel, Glasgow, was said to be an atheist during his younger years as a biochemistry student at Strathclyde University.

But he switched paths after attending a Christmas Eve church service and was ordained two decades ago. He landed his first role in Stirling.



He and Caroline met during a youth mission week.

It is believed she revealed fears just days after their anniversary that he had strayed with a long-time parishioner who has been involved in events at the kirk.

Lyons was seen in a T-shirt and jeans as he left the home provided by the church.

Officials admitted it was a “difficult time for all those involved”.

A Church of Scotland spokesman added: “The circumstances of this case are currently being investigated. We cannot make any further comment at this point.”



Lyons’ Sunday sermons are posted on the church website and YouTube channel.

In one video from April 2023 he preaches to his congregation telling them how marriage can make worshippers “a beacon of light to those around you”.

The most recent footage on the church blog from May shows Lyons conducting a baptism outdoors.

In it, he urges people to use their mobile phones to search for the words ‘I Have Decided to Follow Jesus’ before dunking a church goer in a river.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In other clips he makes jokes about England winning the World Cup and carries out communion wearing a blue hoodie with his church’s PSJ initials on the chest.



He also gave a filmed sermon on the “protection of the heart” and the “unravelling of society”.

News.title: Woman raking in £1k a month in sickness benefits is kinky dominatrix who humiliates clients as ‘maggots’
News.content:
A DOMINATRIX receiving more than £1,000 a month in benefits for conditions including severe disability is selling sexual services on adult websites.

Melanie Bull — also known as Lola Steel and Scarlett Rose — can also make up to an extra £1,000 a month after boasting that she specialises in “financial ­domination”.





She gets PIP payments after demonstrating that her medical condition severely impacts her ability to carry out everyday tasks which can include getting to the bathroom or needing help to eat with a knife and fork.

And the 47-year-old mum of one also gets more state handouts: ­Universal Credit, for having “limited capability” to work, and housing benefit for her rented home.

Yet Miss Bull is not allowing her condition to limit her racy online activities or stop her from going out. In one advert on website UK Adult Zone, she says: “My name is Lola Steel.

“I am a professional mistress who enjoys being a dominant powerful bitch and getting my own way.

“I cover many different fetishes and kinks. I also do phone sessions, text sessions, email sessions.”

And she tells punters online to “step into my world of pleasure”.

Bull gets paid to humiliate so-called male “paypig” clients who send her money and gifts for her pleasure.

A source said: “She makes up to £1,000 a month from a roster of clients who get a sexual thrill from being humiliated. She gets them to send gifts and cash payments.





“The average payment is £20 but she will get them to send one after another so it can be as much as £100 a day.

“The clients call her ‘goddess,’ while she refers to them as ‘paypigs’ and ‘pathetic maggots’. They love her calling them those names. She refers to them as her ­‘findom’ (financial domination) clients.

“Her pictures on the websites she uses are very racy, including showing off her large cleavage.”

Through the UK Adult Zone website, she offers clients an hour-long “in-call” for £110 and for an “out-call” the same length of time it is £150.

On one occasion, according to the source, Bull became concerned when a client gifted her a home delivery of a 55-inch screen TV and she had to leave the box by the bins outside her house in Northamptonshire.

The source added: “She didn’t want to draw any attention to her having money to spend on goods like a large- screen telly, in case it led to ­officials questioning her about her income.”

On another website, called Sadistic Mistress, she goes under the name Scarlett Rose.

Two weeks ago she went to her local pub’s karaoke night where she sang (I’ve Had) The Time Of My Life, from the Dirty Dancing movie, and was also seen out in a cab going into her local city centre.



To qualify to receive PIP she had to convince the Department for Work and Pensions that her medical condition impacts her ability to carry out daily tasks and move around “consistently and safely”.

PIP stands for Personal Independence Payment. It is given out as a benefit to “help with daily living needs and mobility needs”, according to the DWP guidelines. Her condition effectively causes her a disability, she would have claimed.

She also gets some Universal Credit money for having “limited capability” for work.

Sources say her total amount of benefit money is more than £1,000 each month.

Last week Baroness Casey, who is leading a review of welfare and social care, said even she would qualify for disability support based on an official survey by the DWP, as she called for the country to ask ­“difficult questions” on reforming the system.

She pointed out that 16.8million people self-reported a disability in 2023-24, equivalent to one in four British people.

Baroness Casey went on: “I would qualify and I’m sitting here right now. I’m not disabled but I could qualify if I answered those questions based on my medical records.”

The DWP guides that when ­people are receiving any benefit, they must tell DWP if things in their life change as soon as this happens to ensure they receive the correct amount of financial support and do not fall into debt.

This includes any earnings they receive.

Reform UK’s Chairman and MP Lee Anderson told The Sun on Sunday: “This case raises serious questions. PIP should be reserved for those who genuinely need help, yet Labour are allowing the system to be exploited.



“Reform UK would crack down on anyone abusing the system, bring back face-to-face PIP assessments and ensure taxpayers’ money only goes to those who genuinely need it.”

Last night a DWP spokesperson said: “Universal Credit claimants must inform DWP of their earnings. Not doing so can lead to imprisonment.”

Melanie Bull denied being on adult websites.

She declined to comment when asked about being on PIP and Universal Credit.

News.title: Andy Burnham promises crackdown on costly subscription traps and 'rip-off discounts'
News.content:
Andy Burnham promises crackdown on costly subscription traps and 'rip-off discounts'

The Prime Minister will bring forward 'easy to exit' rules, making it less painful for consumers to cancel subscriptions and avoid automatic renewal at a higher cost

View 2 Images Andy Burnham will bring forward 'easy to exit' rules (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Andy Burnham has promised everyday fixes on the cost of living including an end to costly subscription traps and rip-off discounts.

‌



The Prime Minister will bring forward “easy to exit” rules, making it less painful for consumers to cancel subscriptions and avoid automatic renewals at a higher cost. The crackdown was previously unveiled under ex-PM Keir Starmer and is set to include mandatory reminders before renewals of 12-month contracts.

‌



The rules had been due to come into force in Spring 2027, but Mr Burnham will now bring forward by several months to January in time for when customers often start new subscriptions. Downing Street has said it will save consumers an estimated £400 million - or £14 each month per unwanted subscription.

‌



Andy Burnham kicks off summer tour of UK to hear from voters on cost of living READ MORE :

Voters say mental health support over benefit cuts is best way to get young back into work READ MORE :

View 2 Images Andy Burnham has said his government wants to put more money in people's pockets (Image: Getty Images)

No10 also said “pretend prices and deceptive deals will be a thing of the past” under new proposals. They said the Prime Minister plans to ban retailers from making misleading claims to customers about discounts after complaints prices are being artificially hiked to give a false sense of value.

Mr Burnham said: “I know people are sick and tired of rip-off discounts and subscription traps. Westminster has got used to telling people that everyday hassles like this are just part of life.

‌



“I don’t think that’s right, especially when the cost of living continues to weigh heavily on so many people’s lives. I’m determined to pull every single lever we can to provide people with some room to breathe on the cost of living.”

He added: “We’re putting an end to phoney bargains. If something is advertised as half price, it should actually be half price. We’re also making it as easy to leave a subscription as it is to join.

“These are just two of the everyday fixes we’re going to be rolling out – today is just the start. We want to put more money in people’s pockets and give people hope that politics really can work for them and their everyday lives.”

Article continues below

Chief executive of Citizens Advice, Dame Clare Moriarty, said: “For too long consumers have been tricked into paying for products or services they don’t use - or didn’t even want to begin with - costing millions of pounds each year. So we really welcome the government’s move to speed up action on subscription traps and look at banning other tactics firms use to catch consumers out.”

She added: “At Citizens Advice, we’ve sounded the alarm on this for years, because we know subscription traps and sneaky online practices that hit consumers’ pockets hard are a widespread problem. We previously found that over 13 million people (26% of UK adults) accidentally took out a subscription in a year.”

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds added: “There’s nothing worse than realising you’ve been fleeced by a dodgy deal, or seen money leaving your account because of a subscription you didn’t want to renew or couldn’t easily cancel. This Government is on the side of families working hard to make ends meet, while making sure the rules are clear for businesses and easy to follow.”

News.title: Voters say mental health support over benefit cuts is best way to get young back into work
News.content:
Voters say mental health support over benefit cuts is best way to get young back into work

EXCLUSIVE: The survey for More in Common found the most popular measure for getting young people with mental health conditions back into work is to increase access to support

View 2 Images Over a million young people are currently out of work, education or training (Image: Getty Images)

Voters believe faster access to mental health support over cuts to benefits is the best way to get young people back to work.

‌



The finding in a survey for More in Common pollsters comes ahead of a major report into fixing the ‘Neets’ crisis by the former Labour Cabinet minister Alan Milburn in the autumn. New Prime Minister Andy Burnham has also declared it a “mission” to reduce the over one million 18-24-year-olds not in employment, education, or training.

‌



According to the survey shared with The Mirror, a majority of all voters believe many young people are out of work because it is too easy to claim benefits instead of working. But the conclusion was not shared by 18-24-year-olds, the results show.

‌



Andy Burnham kicks off summer tour of UK to hear from voters on cost of living READ MORE :

View 2 Images Ex-Labour Cabinet minister Alan Milburn is leading a review of Neets (Image: Joe Giddens/PA Wire)

A majority (51%) of respondents in this age bracket said many were out of employment due to mental health problems genuinely preventing them from working. The survey also found the most popular measure for getting young people with mental health conditions back into work is to increase access to support.

‌



Respondents were asked to select up to two responses, and the statement with the largest share on 40% was faster access to mental health treatment. Other options including requirements to look for work, more support from employers, and reducing benefits, all came in joint second on 30%. Just over 22% said better training and qualifications.

Alongside the report into the ‘Neets’ crisis, Sir Stephen Timms, the DWP minister, is also expected to publish a separate review on reform of Personal Independence Payments (PIP) this autumn. He warned last month the main disability benefit, which was introduced in 2013 to help towards the extra costs of disability and support independent living, was “not fit for purpose”.

It was ordered last year after ex-PM Keir Starmer was forced to rip up plans to slash £5billion from sickness and disability benefits in the wake of a major Labour rebellion. UK director of More in Common Luke Tryl said: “The public don’t need convincing that there is a real problem with young people and worklessness.

‌



“Nearly two in three Britons say many young people are out of work because it has become too easy to claim benefits, and a majority say the bigger problem with PIP is that it is going to people who do not need it - a view shared by nearly half of Labour’s own 2024 voters. The public has an appetite for reform to get the benefits bill down.

“ But while the public agree with that diagnosis, their prescription is not simply cuts, but often greater support. Asked what would do most to get young people with mental health conditions into work, the answer chosen most often is faster access to mental health treatment - ahead of tougher conditions or reducing what people can claim.”

“That is the balance Burnham’s Government may need to tread as the Timms Review reports this autumn. Britons want a welfare system that gets people back to work, but they also want to ensure that mental health support is there for those who need it.”

Article continues below

Writing for The Mirror earlier this week - as the government announced the next phase in the roll-out of new mental health units - Mr Burnham also warned of “a profound mental health crisis impacting younger generations”. But he added: "There are those who are quick to criticise young people today, but that’s never been my way. Our country’s future depends on them – and they will have this government’s support.

“The overwhelming majority of the one million young people not in education, employment or training want the chance to build their future. But poor mental health, combined with a system that can’t keep up, robs them of that opportunity. These new NHS facilities will help get lives moving again.”

::: More in Common polled a representative weighted sample of 3,384 GB adults between July 31 and August 2, 2026

News.title: Andy Burnham kicks off summer tour of UK to hear from voters on cost of living
News.content:
Andy Burnham kicks off summer tour of UK to hear from voters on cost of living

EXCLUSIVE: Prime Minister Andy Burnham tells The Mirror he'll be spending the month 'out of Westminster and into your town' to ask people 'what would actually make your life better?'

View 3 Images PM Andy Burnham is expected to spend the rest of the summer on the road (Image: Getty Images)

Andy Burnham is set to kickstart a summer tour of the country this week and ask voters directly: "What would actually make your life better?"

‌



The new Prime Minister, who returns from a short holiday abroad this week, is expected to spend the rest of August on the road visiting every nation and region across Britain. In the coming days he is also set to outline measures to tackle misleading discounts and rip-off prices while promising action to get high streets thriving again.

‌



Mr Burnham told The Mirror: “This month I'm out of Westminster and into your town. Not for the photographs, but because I want to hear directly from people in their communities. I'll be asking one question: what would actually make your life better?

‌



View 3 Images Andy Burnham reintroduced the £2 cap on bus fares in his first week as PM (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

“We know a lot of the issues. People have been saying it for years and no one listened. Bills that land like a threat. A high street of shuttered units and rip-off prices.”

He added: "So here is what's coming. A third off bus fares. VAT off your electricity bill. Action next week on misleading discounts and pricing tricks. We're putting money back in people's pockets and giving communities the power they need to thrive. Good growth in every postcode. Hope in every heart.”

‌



As he returns from a short summer holiday this week, Mr Burnham is expected to renew his focus on the cost of living and travel around the nation before Parliament returns in early September. Insiders confirmed among the places the new Labour leader will visit will be Port Talbot, south Wales - an area reeling from over 2,000 job losses after the closure of a final blast furnace.

Reports have previously suggested Mr Burnham could head to parts of the country where his party has lost support in recent years including areas that voted Reform in 2024. No10 said he will sit down with families, shop owners and workers during the tour.

The visits will ultimately inform his work on a new 10-year plan for the country that Mr Burnham promised later this year in his first speech as Prime Minister. He said at the time it would lay out a “path from where we are now to where I believe we all want Britain to be” later in 2026.

‌



It follows a policy blitz in his first week in Downing with measures designed to give cash-strapped families breathing space on the cost of living. This included a promise to remove the VAT charged on electricity bills from October 1 - estimated to cost £850million - to knock £45 off the average bill.

There was also the decision to reintroduce the £2 bus fare cap to slash day-to-day travel costs for millions of passengers across England from January. The £2 cap was first introduced by the Tories in 2023, but funding was only put in place by Rishi Sunak ’s government until the end of 2024.

View 3 Images Andy Burnham at No10 North in Manchester during his first week as Prime Minister (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Ex-Chancellor Rachel Reeves hiked it to £3 as she battled to balance the books. The current cap, which applies to around 5,000 bus routes across England, was planned to last until March 2027.

In his second week as PM, Mr Burnham also began to grapple with some of the thorniest issues facing Britain including the broken social care sector, defence spending, and the staggering number of young people out of work, education and training. The PM has established No10 North in Manchester which Downing Street said was set up to get the government out of the Westminster bubble.

The summer tour - expected to begin this week - also comes amid evidence of a “Burnham bounce” in the national polls and closing the gap on Nigel Farage ’s Reform UK. Elections expert Professor Sir John Curtice told the BBC last week it was confirmed by Labour's comfortable victory in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election, where Reform had been hoping for a major political upset in Labour's traditional heartland.

Article continues below

Sir John added: "Polls conducted in the last week put Labour on average in the mid 20s. It is the party's highest standing since the beginning of last year and compares to their rating of 19% in late June when Sir Keir Starmer announced he was standing down. But with Reform polling only narrowly behind Labour, Burnham's party still has a long way to go before it can face the prospect of fighting a general election with confidence."

News.title: 'Coronation Street' rapist's cause of death behind bars confirmed
News.content:
'Coronation Street' rapist's cause of death behind bars confirmed

Andrew Davies, dubbed 'The Coronation Street rapist,' was handed 13 life sentences for raping 13 women and an additional 56 years for other offences after striking terror across the north

View 3 Images Andrew Davies, from Bolton, targeted lone women (Image: MEN)

The cause of death of a serial predator, who struck terror across the north of England, has been confirmed.

‌



Andrew Davies, from Bolton, targeted lone women after waiting for their husbands or fathers to leave the property in the morning.

‌



Davies, formerly known as Andrew Barlow and Andrew Longmire was given 13 life sentences for his vile crimes in 1988. He was released in 2023 after 34 years in prison, but was recalled to prison just six weeks later.

‌



The decision to release Davies, known as ‘the Coronation Street rapist,’ sparked public fury and the then Justice Secretary Dominic Raab intervened in a bid to prevent it. Just weeks after his release he was recalled to prison for breach of his licence conditions.

View 3 Images Davies, formerly known as Andrew Barlow and Andrew Longmire was given 13 life sentences for his crimes (Image: MEN)

News of Davies' death was reported in February this year but now a report by the Prisons and Probation Ombudsman has disclosed further details.

‌



Davies died from natural causes after contracting brain cancer, the Manchester Evening News reports. The report states: "In October 2017, Mr Andrew Davies was sentenced to life imprisonment for sexual offences. He died of brain cancer on 28 February 2026, at HMP Moorland. He was 69 years old. We offer our condolences to Mr Davies’ family and friends.

"The Ombudsman’s office wrote to Mr Davies’ next of kin to explain the investigation and to ask if they had any matters they wanted us to consider. They did not respond.

"One prisoner contacted us and raised concerns about the care Mr Davies received at Moorland. NHS England commissioned an independent clinical reviewer to review Mr Davies’ clinical care at Moorland.

‌



View 3 Images Andrew Davies, from Bolton, targeted lone women (Image: MEN)

"The clinical reviewer concluded that the clinical care Mr Davies received at Moorland was of a reasonable standard and was equivalent to that which he could have expected to receive in the community. She made four recommendations on issues unrelated to Mr Davies’ death which the Head of Healthcare will wish to address.

"The PPO investigator investigated the non-clinical issues relating to Mr Davies’ care. We did not find any non-clinical issues of concern. We make no recommendations. We shared our initial report with HMPPS and the prison’s healthcare provider, Practice Plus Group.

‌



"They found no factual inaccuracies. At the inquest, held on 8 April 2026, the Coroner concluded that Mr Davies died from natural causes."

Barlow was handed 11 life sentences in for raping 11 women and an additional 56 years for other offences at a 1988 trial. In 2010, and then again in 2017, he received two more life sentences after rapes he committed in 1981 and 1982 which were linked to him through advances in DNA technology.

As he had already surpassed his original 20-year tariff imposed in 1988 just another two years were added to his sentence in each case.

Article continues below

He was dubbed 'The Coronation Street rapist' as most of the victims were attacked in their own terraced homes in the north of England, the majority living in Greater Manchester. Two of the attacks took place in the street. He also struck in Cheshire, Staffordshire, Lancashire, and South Yorkshire in the early 1980s, and then again from August 1987 until January 1988 when he was arrested.

Barlow was sought by police in the 1980s over 11 of the rapes. During the hunt for him he evaded police at Leeds railway station and went on to shoot at two officers when he was finally arrested in Bebington, Merseyside. The officers were not injured and Longmire was later convicted of their attempted murder.

News.title: Man accused of Brit's suitcase murder in Greece 'turned back on faith' before her death
News.content:
Man accused of Brit's suitcase murder in Greece 'turned back on faith' before her death

The body of Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, was discovered in a suitcase in a derelict building in Athens on July 18, and Afghan refugee and Christian convert Sharif Ahmadzai has been charged with her murder

View 4 Images Sharif Ahmadzai, who is suspected of killing Elisabeth-Jane Ross, and his wife Alaina Hall (Image: FACEBOOK)

The man accused of killing British woman Elisabeth-Jane Ross, who was found dead inside a suitcase in Greece, reportedly “turned his back on his Christian faith” before her death.

Afghan boxer Sharif Ahmadzai has been charged with homicide with intent over the death of 38-year-old Elisabeth-Jane, known as Lisa, whose body was discovered inside a suitcase in a derelict building in Athens on July 18.

The claims about Ahmadzai's faith and behaviour before Lisa's death have been reported by the Daily Mail, which spoke to two evangelical Christians who said his wife Alaina Hall had confided in them about concerns she had regarding her husband's changing behaviour.

According to the newspaper, Alaina told the pair that Ahmadzai had become more distant from his Christian faith and was spending more time boxing and with friends. The sources also claimed she had become concerned about him spending time in bars in Athens.

View 4 Images Elisabeth Jane Ross, also known as Lisa, was found by a homeless man on July 18 (Image: Facebook)

Ahmadzai fled Afghanistan in 2016 and is understood to have converted to Christianity after meeting Alaina through charity work in Greece. The couple run a charity called Love Every Nation, which supports homeless people and refugees in Athens.

Lisa had also been carrying out charity work in Greece as a Christian aid worker and had met Alaina through volunteering and church meetings. Alaina told investigators she and Lisa had become friends after meeting in February.

She reportedly told police she last saw Lisa on July 12. When she later asked her husband when he had seen Lisa, he allegedly said they had last spoken on July 15, when Lisa had asked him to accompany her while delivering a Bible.

Alaina also reportedly told investigators that she woke shortly after midnight on July 15 and found Ahmadzai was not at home. She said she checked his location on her mobile phone.

Ahmadzai was initially arrested on weapons offences before prosecutors charged him with homicide with intent. He also faces allegations of stealing more than €10,000 (around £8,500) from Lisa's bank accounts using her bank cards.

View 4 Images Sharif Ahmadzai was a keen boxer (Image: INSTAGRAM)

Greek authorities say Ahmadzai has admitted moving Lisa's body but denies killing her.

His lawyer, Christos Erdos, confirmed his client did not answer questions during Thursday's hearing.

Following the hearing, a judge ordered Ahmadzai to remain in pre-trial detention while prosecutors continue gathering evidence ahead of future court proceedings. The allegations against Ahmadzai have not been proven in court.

He was later escorted from court by masked police officers and driven away.

Investigators previously said Ahmadzai became a suspect after officers examined CCTV footage recorded close to where Lisa's body was discovered.

View 4 Images Elisabeth Jane Ross was reportedly known to Sharif Ahmadzai through his wife Alaina Hall (Image: Facebook)

Police believe she died several days before she was found, during a period when temperatures in Athens reached 36C. She was formally identified using fingerprint evidence.

Article continues below

Lisa travelled to Greece on June 26 and had initially been staying with friends in the port district of Piraeus.

The Foreign and Commonwealth Office said earlier: “Our thoughts are with Elisabeth’s family during this difficult time. We are providing consular support and are in contact with the local authorities.”

A Police Scotland spokesperson previously said: “We are aware of the death of a Scottish woman in Athens and are liaising with authorities in Greece. Officers are providing support to her family in Scotland.”

News.title: Internet sensation Ibiza Final Boss set to launch his own hair styling range
News.content:
Internet sensation Ibiza Final Boss set to launch his own hair styling range

A builder with a bowl cut nicknamed the Ibiza Final Boss after going viral last summer plans to launch his own haircare range.

Jack Kay, 26, became an internet sensation when he was filmed partying on the Spanish island with his distinctive hairdo. He has now managed to trademark the words “Final Boss” for a string of potions including hair styling spray, wax, gel, mousse and shampoo.

The papers, approved by the Intellectual Property Office, also give him the scope to create hair dyes, hair masks, and beard oil moisturiser. Footage emerged online of Kay boogying at Wayne Lineker’s O Beach Club last year.

Ibiza Final Boss' unlikely friendship with new mentor Anthony Joshua READ MORE :

Ibiza Final Boss and Jordan McCann agree huge purse for boxing rematch READ MORE :

With his chunky gold chain, designer sunglasses, black vest, and his signature bowl cut, he became the subject of thousands of online comments.
