President Donald Trump’s Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, General Dan Caine, is seeking an “off-ramp “ from the ongoing war in Iran, according to a new report.

Caine has privately told other top administration officials that the country needs to find a way to exit the war, according to CNN, which cited three sources familiar with the matter.

Despite Trump claiming throughout the war that a peace deal, which would include his demand that Iran never obtain a nuclear weapon, was within reach, fighting has continued for more than five months.

“Caine is looking for an off ramp,” one of CNN’s sources said.

The general’s meetings with Trump officials, including Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, are just to make clear the limitations and pitfalls of different military options, according to the sources.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump’s Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, General Dan Caine, is seeking an 'off-ramp' from the ongoing war in Iran, according to a new report ( Getty Images )

“We do not discuss the Chairman’s confidential conversations with the President, the Secretary, or other senior leaders, nor do we comment on anonymous, agenda-driven characterizations of those conversations by sources who were not privy to them,” Joseph Holstead, a spokesperson for Caine, told CNN.

A White House official praised Caine’s know-how, calling him an “incredible asset to President Trump’s national security team.”

“The General always provides accurate, unbiased information and a host of options to the Commander-in-Chief, who ultimately makes decisions based on what he feels is best for US national security”, the official said.

A spokesperson for Caine decline to comment to The Independent.

A U.S. official also condemned what they called “agenda-driven leaders” who “cherry picks” information in an attempt to create the appearance of division among senior leaders.

open image in gallery The Iran war, which is both costly and unpopular with Americans, has dragged on for more than five months ( AFP via Getty Images )

Trump’s war has primarily been an air campaign, relying on fighters to launch strikes against Iran instead of deploying ground troops. Caine and other Trump officials privately think it's unlikely that an air campaign alone can put enough pressure on the Iranians to agree to a deal that’s favorable to the president, according to multiple people familiar with recent discussions who spoke with CNN.

Meanwhile, Trump has denied recent reports that the U.S. military’s weapons stockpile is dwindling.

“The U.S. has massive amounts of ‘munitions,’ especially of certain types. Additionally, large amounts are being manufactured and shipped to the U.S. as needed. Defense companies are building the largest number of plants and factories in our country’s history.

“The ‘leakers’ of these treasonous statements are being hunted down. Long term jail sentences will be sought!” Trump wrote on Truth Social Thursday.

Trump’s threats came after Reuters reported Tuesday, citing two unnamed sources, that the Army has used “virtually all” of its long-range Army Tactical Missile Systems and Precision Strike Missiles.

A recent report has also found that the Pentagon is running low on missile interceptors.

The U.S. military had 2,330 Patriot systems and 452 Terminal High Altitude Area Defense systems before the war, according to the report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies. As of July 27, an estimated 759 to 827 Patriot systems and 234 to 278 THAAD systems remain, the report said.

open image in gallery Despite Trump claiming throughout the war that a peace deal was within reach, fighting has dragged on ( Getty Images )

During a Senate Appropriations Committee hearing last month, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said U.S. military operations in Iran have cost an estimated $37.5 billion. He also asked Congress for an additional $67 billion to, in part, replenish weapons stockpiles, blaming the Biden administration for not properly funding the Pentagon.

The price of gas has also surged during the war, sitting above $4 a gallon Friday, according to motor club AAA. The price of a gallon of gas was just below $3 at the start of the war, according to the Associated Press.

Just 28 percent of Americans said they approved of Trump’s handling of Iran in a new Reuters/Ipsos poll.

News.title: Argentina v South Africa LIVE: Result and reaction as Springboks cling on for victory but Kolisi injured
News.content:
( AP )

South Africa just about clung on for a 17-10 victory over a depleted Argentina in Buenos Aires – though were dealt a huge injury scare ahead of four Tests against New Zealand.

The Springboks continued their winning streak with a hard-fought win secured by a last goalline stand on a day where both sides failed to fire in attack and defences dominated. Argentina, missing plenty of regular starters, could take huge credit from a strong showing though were left to rue a series of missed opportunities and a faltering second-half set-piece.

Rassie Erasmus will not have been best pleased by the overall Springboks showing with the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series against the All Blacks to come over the next few weeks, and watched Siya Kolisi limp off in the first half. Will the captain be fit for the marquee matches against New Zealand?

Follow all of the latest from the international clash with our live blog below:

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

News.title: Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan
News.content:
Chelsea 3 AC Milan 0

Chelsea cruised to a 3-0 victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head intothe break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto. Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

News.title: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong
News.content:
Aston Villa 1 Bayern Munich 2

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.title: The best luxury hotels in the Cotswolds
News.content:
From gracious old farmsteads and magnificent manor houses to an ancient coaching inn creaking with Tudor character, the top luxury hotels in the Cotswolds combine a wonderful sense of history with contemporary style and outstanding modern British cuisine. Whether near picturesque Broadway in the north of the region or close to Bath in the south, location is a key attribute to them all: some offer serene escapes in acres of their own rolling parkland; others sit amid superb gardens; and several take over classic honey-stone villages that look as if they have been beamed in from a halcyon era of the past.

They all excel in providing creature comforts, whether crackling fires by kick-back sofas, canopy beds with soft throws, or suites with terraces and hot tubs. Facilities are top-notch too, ranging from beautiful bars and quiet terraces to blissful spas with inviting pools and even an opportunity for equine adventures. Read on to discover our pick of the best luxury hotels in the Cotswolds.

News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

Sports.title: Phil Foden’s girlfriend flogging Three Lions shirts on Vinted after he was dropped by Tuchel
Sports.content:
SNUBBED England ace Phil Foden’s girlfriend is flogging new Three Lions shirts on Vinted — after her World Cup trip with other Wags did not go ahead.

Rebecca Cooke, 25, offers two shirts on the second-hand website for £70 each — the latest white home and red away strips.



The jerseys were modified by a clothing brand which tightened the waists for women.

Other England Wags who did make it to the US and Mexico for the World Cup wore the same tops — including Ollie Watkins’ wife Ellie and Anthony Gordon’s girlfriend Annie Keating.



The tops — both in size 12-14 — are listed as being “new with tags”.

They have been modified by Essex-based company A Vintage Fit.

The shirts cost £89.99 on the official England website and the firm charges £90 each to adapt them into a figure-hugging version.

Mum-of-three Rebecca’s England tops are among more than 100 items for sale on her Vinted page.

Also included are four cinched Man City tops — including last season’s grey and bright green third kit for £70 in “perfect condition”.

Two City shirts are vintage from retro footie kit firm Score Draw.



Rebecca’s account states: “Selling new & used authentic items only. Account ran by management team.”



It was not known if she donates to charity any money raised through Vinted.

She had been expecting to go to this year’s World Cup tournament with £15million-a-year Man City star Phil, 26.

He was devastated at being dropped by manager Thomas Tuchel.

A source said: “Perhaps Rebecca had one foot on the plane when she got the tops.”

We approached Rebecca and Phil for comment.



Under-fire Fifa boss Gianni Infantino was last night facing new pressure after it was alleged he paid off a mistress in his job as a Uefa executive.

He denies the allegations.

Sports.title: Barcelona set to launch new bid for Man City superstar Rodri with Enzo Maresca’s side demanding £60million transfer fee
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY boss Enzo Maresca is braced for a new Barcelona bid for Rodri.

The LaLiga champions are sure the midfielder wants to join them this summer.



An offer of £38.5million for Spain’s World Cup-winning captain was laughed off by Etihad chiefs on Friday.

City believe the 30-year-old former Ballon d’Or winner is worth more than £60m — despite having less than 12 months remaining on his current contract.



But Barca transfer guru Deco is ready to test the resolve of the Prem side again, with confidence high at the Nou Camp that they can get a deal done this month.

Rodri, who has been in the North West for the last seven years, is believed to be keen to return to his homeland.

Despite having minor back surgery a couple of weeks ago, he is due back at his current employers this week.

Maresca’s men finish their Far East tour with a game against the midfielder’s old club Atletico Madrid on Sunday.

They will then fly back to Manchester and, by Wednesday, the new boss expects to have his full squad in training at the City Football Academy.

Whether that will include Rodri remains to be seen, with Barcelona determined to get their man despite their recent financial problems.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Meanwhile, City will be on the look-out for a replacement if Rodri does go.

Even though Nico Gonzalez, who they signed for £50m in January last year, plays in a similar position.

The Etihad giants have already spent £116m on Elliot Anderson and are hoping to complete a move for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, the Morocco ace, 18, valued at £85m.

Antoine Semenyo and Marc Guehi have also arrived this year but question marks remain over Rodri and winger Savinho.

Sports.title: Famous napkin contract and Real Madrid transfer threat – How Lionel Messi’s dad guided son through iconic career
Sports.content:
JORGE MESSI died in Rosario aged 68 on Friday night following a long battles with illness.

A driving force behind son Lionel’s outstanding career, tributes poured in for Jorge.



Barcelona expressed their “deepest condolences”, while Jorge’s beloved Newell’s Old Boys spoke of their “deep sorrow and grief”.

A former steel factory worker, Jorge went on to play a huge role in arguably the greatest football career of all time.



He sent Leo, the youngest of three brothers and older sibling to sister Maria Sol, to play for Newell’s from the age of six.

The future superstar obviously immediately oozed talent, but suffered from a growth hormone deficiency which threatened to kibosh his career before it had even started.

When Newell’s stopped paying for treatment, Jorge knew that he had to do something.

He convinced Barcelona to take a look at his son, and accompanied his 14-year-old boy to Europe as he took part in a two-week trial with the Catalan giants in September 2001.



Then-Barca director Carles Rexach was convinced, Leo’s talent was obvious.

But with the LaLiga giants in financial peril at the time, other club chiefs hesitated over whether the swoop for Messi was worth what was considered such a large expense at the time.

Sweating over his son’s growth hormones treatment, which still needed to be paid for, Jorge began looking at other potential moves.



He had been turned down by Argentine giants River Plate, but Real Madrid and Atletico began to circle.

At a now-legendary meeting at a tennis club in December 2001, the deal to bring Messi to Barca was sealed… via a napkin.

Speaking to ESPN, Rexach recalled: “Jorge thought [Barca] were stalling. I wasn’t there and don’t know exactly how things were, but when I met with Jorge I realised he wasn’t clear on anything.

“I suppose he didn’t trust [Barca] and he seemed desperate, so one night I met with [Josep Maria] Minguella and Horacio [Gaggioli] at the Pompeya tennis club and, speaking with Jorge on the phone, he told me, ‘If this isn’t sorted soon, we’re going. I have to return to Buenos Aires and I don’t see anything happening.’

“That was when, thinking on my feet, I decided everything.”



Rexach wrote on a napkin, in Spanish: “In Barcelona, on Dec. 14, 2000, in the presence of Minguella and Horacio, Carles Rexach, FC Barcelona’s sporting director, hereby agrees, under his responsibility and regardless of any dissenting opinions, to sign the player Lionel Messi provided that we keep to the amounts agreed upon.”

The document, which was legally binding, if unorthodox, was signed by Rexach and other Barca chiefs Minguella and Gaggioli – and went on to be flogged at auction two years ago for a staggering £762,400.

From this point onwards, Jorge was his son’s agent, confidante and father rolled into one.



As Leo’s mother Celia and three siblings returned to Rosario, Jorge stayed with his golden child in Barcelona – even insisting that his boy live with him in a city apartment, rather than boarding with the other kids at La Masia.

Messi told Radio del Plata in 2007: “My dad was always by my side.

“Sometimes I would lock myself in my room to cry when we arrived in Barcelona, or my dad would do the same without me seeing him, or thinking I didn’t see him.

“We pretended we were both OK, but we weren’t. My dad even asked me what I wanted to do when we were feeling down, if I wanted to stay or go back, and I wanted to stay, and he stayed with me.”

While Messi progressed through La Masia, Jorge negotiated his first professional contract in 2004, before Barca were forced to fend off significant interest from Inter Milan two years later.



As Leo’s star rose, so did his earning potential – and without a super-agent in tow, it was down to Jorge to capitalise.

The Argentine has had lucrative deals with the likes of Adidas, Pepsi, Budweiser and Konami, to name just a few, during his brilliant career.

In 2017, Jorge negotiated a four-year, €555 million contract, worth around £480m at the time, making his son the highest-paid athlete EVER.



Leo then went on to spend two forgettable seasons at Paris Saint-Germain, before Jorge assisted in another landmark deal three years ago.

In addition to his basic salary at Inter Miami, Messi takes a cut of Apple TV’s broadcast deal with MLS, which is claimed to be worth around $50m (£37m) to the global icon.

Also in 2023, investment firm Play Time was launched – yet another revenue stream for Brand Messi.

Jorge suffered with a long-term illness prior to his death, and was unable to watch his boy at the World Cup this summer – a factor that is thought to have contributed to Messi’s emotional outburst during his side’s opening victory of the tournament.

Leo’s father leaves behind a huge legacy as the man that brought up the greatest footballer of all time.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Newell’s fitting tribute read: “Jorge was the support and the person who, together with his wife, Celia, strengthened the career of the greatest player of all time with vision, rigour and affection.

“His constant support and behind-the-scenes leadership were fundamental in supporting every step of Lionel’s journey.”

Sports.title: Not that close, hey!’ – Erling Haaland turns into ‘jealous boyfriend’ as actor chats with stunning girlfriend Isabel
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY superstar Erling Haaland jokingly turned into a jealous boyfriend in a clip circling on social media.

Italian actor Michele Morrone was seen chatting to Haaland‘s girlfriend Isabel Johansen.



As his partner and Morrone chatted, Haaland said to the camera: “Hey, hey, hey.

“Not that close, not that close.”



However his huge grin immediately afterwards indicated that the big Norwegian was just messing around.

The viral clip came from a video on Haaland’s YouTube channel, where his girlfriend Isabel features regularly.



The Norse raider posted vlog content during the World Cup in the USA, as Norway reached the quarter-finals for the first ever time.

Martin Odegaard, Haaland and Co were eventually stopped by England thanks to a Jude Bellingham double.

The players and fans started the iconic Norway ‘row’ at the World Cup, emulating the behaviour of their Viking ancestors.

Prior to the tournament the team found themselves in hot water with some members of the Norwegian public, as their Viking-style photoshoot was slammed by factions of the country’s media.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

However, the Norway faithful embraced the Viking way as they rowed and rowed all the way to the quarters.

Haaland has evidently continued with his YouTube side-hustle ahead of the beginning of the new Premier League season.

Sports.title: Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle in fiery debut brawl vs Valencia as Anthony Elanga stretchered off after horror tackle
Sports.content:
MATTHIAS JAISSLE kicked off his Newcastle reign with a brawl against ten-man Valencia.

The German, 38, was fuming as opposition skipper Jose Luis Gaya produced a horror tackle on Anthony Elanga just yards away.



Toon’s new boss instantly raced towards the linesman demanding red – which duly arrived – as players from both sides got into a mini-brawl.

Swedish winger Elanga, Newcastle’s most impressive performer, was eventually stretchered off to cap off an already nightmare start.



Less than four minutes were on the clock when Filip Ugrinic was given all the time in the world to curl home from 25 yards.

Both sides were forced into a reshuffle following Gaya’s red card.



Following the lengthy delay, Jacob Murphy replaced Elanga.

SunSport understands that Elanga suffered a shin contusion, but that it is not as bad as first feared.

He was up and walking not long after the scare, with Newcastle going on to win 2-1.

The Swede would have been looking to impress his new boss Jaissle, having struggled to produce his best form under Howe last term.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Elanga scored three goals and laid on one assist in 49 appearances in his debut Toon campaign.

The year before at Nottingham Forest he had managed six goals and 12 assists.

Newcastle have three friendlies remaining; against Everton, Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg.

They will then begin their Prem campaign by hosting Liverpool on August 23.



And the following week will see them quickly reunite with former star Sandro Tonali, as they travel to North London to face Tottenham.

As for the game against Valencia, Yoanne Wissa was at the double as he and new signing Bazouma Toure stole the show to seal a 2-1 victory in Jaissle’s first game.

This week at Toon’s pre-season La Manga camp, club officials boasted about sprint records being broken in training under the German coach with “intensity” a particular buzzword.

But less than four minutes were on the clock when Filip Ugrinic was given all the time in the world to curl home from 25 yards.

A good strike but Newcastle will need more from new No1 Lukas Hornicek, who joined on Monday in a £25.7m move, once the real stuff gets underway.



Miscommunication with Sven Botman almost led to the defender heading over the onrushing ‘keeper for a second too, only for the ball to bounce a yard wide and out for a corner.

Newcastle wanted a penalty when Will Osula was sent tumbling by Gaya and Elanga had a goal ruled out for offside before his night was cut short.

But it was that moment that changed the game. Fuelled by anger over the tackle and with a man advantage, we began to see glimpses of the “high-energy football” fans had been promised.

Wissa, desperate to impress after a shocking first season at the club, got the goal seven minutes after coming on at the break.



Fellow sub Toure, the £42.5m replacement from Hoffenheim for Gordon down the left wing, forced a defender into panickingly trying to pass back to his goalkeeper. Wissa was on the loose ball in a flash, charging through and slipping it past Stole Dimitrievski’s legs.

The livewire winger provided another scare and needed treatment for a shoulder issue after a tumble before racing through to tee-up Wissa for a tap-in.

There are still plenty of issues for Jaissle, one being the Nick Woltemade conundrum. The head coach showed more energy racing around in front of his dugout and barking out orders than his gangly German striker did in his No10 role. It was his slackness that allowed Ugrinic to pull the trigger for the opener.

But at least Toure’s display provided some chink of light following what has been a bruising summer for the Toon Army.

Speaking after, Jaissle said: “We will not smash the locker room now and celebrate a lot, we’re quite balanced. We know what it is about. Now it’s pre-season and we still have a lot to work on.



“First of all, I’m really happy that there are no serious injuries. Anthony, we are happy and it seems to be not serious. That’s the most important thing and, of course, winning games helps always to gain confidence.

“But we also knew that we had a hard week behind us. The players did well in the camp. There was a clear commitment to see in each session. We had a hard load, so therefore now they deserve two days off, and then we start again.”

Asked whether his young summer signings are ready to face Liverpool in the Premier League opener in a fortnight, he added: “That’s already too long ahead to think about now if you ask me about the starting eleven for Liverpool.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I’m just here now a couple of days. We have still three more friendly matches where we will see many things and that’s our goal, just to give everyone the chance to show up.

“And if you ask me about the three signings, I was not involved, that was before my time, as you know, so, but I’m happy that they’re here.”

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford pictured partying with bikini-clad women on luxury boat as he shares £270 a bottle champagne & sips beer
Sports.content:
FOOTBALLER Marcus Rashford becomes Flash Rash on holiday as he throws his cash around for a group of girls on a luxury boat.

The England and Man Utd star shared a £270 bottle of Armand de Brignac Brut Gold champagne with pals.



He also wore an expensive pair of Louis Vuitton trainers, a chunky silver chain with a pendant that reads “Home is where the heart is” and a £23,000 black Hublot Square Bang Unico watch.

The 28-year-old, said to be paid £325,000 a week, enjoyed his post-World Cup break on a hired boat on the French Riviera with ten female pals — but with no sign of his girlfriend, Lucia Loi.



A witness said: “The England lads played so well at the World Cup and deserve some downtime after a heroic third-place finish.

“It was kind of Marcus to share his time off with a group of stunning women on the ocean waves. He’s really living the dream.”





After a year-long loan to Spanish La Liga side Barcelona, Rashford is set for a return to boyhood club United for the new Premier League season, starting later this month.

He is due to re-join Michael Carrick’s outfit next week, but has also been linked with an £80million transfer to clubs including Arsenal and Spurs.

Rashford made his debut for United aged 18 in 2016 and went on to make 426 appearances in all competitions.

But he has not pulled on a United shirt since the Europa League tie against Czech side Viktoria Plzen in December 2024 and fell out with former Red Devils boss Ruben Amorim.

When Amorim left him out of the team for an 11th successive game, the manager said he would rather play his 63-year-old goalkeeping coach Jorge Vital than Rashford.



Amorim was in a stand-off with the England international, who previously declared he wanted a “new challenge” away from the club he had spent more than a decade representing.



United sacked Amorim on January 5, 2026, after 14 months in charge, following a 1–1 draw against Leeds United and growing tensions with the club hierarchy.

Rashford could make his return in a pre-season friendly against Leeds in Dublin on Wednesday.

Then on Saturday, United play AC Milan — where Amorim is now the manager.

Sports.title: Man Utd forced to field unknown keeper who last played in non-league FOUR YEARS ago after injury crisis in PSG friendly
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED were forced to turn to little-known goalkeeper Dermot Mee after their injury crisis deepened against Paris Saint-Germain.

The 24-year-old was thrown into the action during United’s 1-1 pre-season draw with the Champions League winners in Gothenburg after Tom Heaton pulled up injured.



Heaton raced from his goal to make a clearance early in the second half before immediately grabbing the back of his right hamstring.

The veteran stopper was unable to continue, leaving United with little choice but to call upon academy graduate Mee.



And incredibly, Mee’s only senior competitive appearances came FOUR YEARS ago during a loan spell with non-league Altrincham in the National League.

The Birmingham-born keeper, who has represented Northern Ireland at youth level, has been on United’s books since the age of 11.

He has become a regular presence around the first-team training set-up in recent years while also representing the Red Devils at Under-21 level.

United clearly value Mee’s contribution behind the scenes, with the stopper recently signing a new two-year contract at Old Trafford.

But he would hardly have expected to be called upon against the kings of Europe.

And the goalkeeper headache was just one of several injury and disciplinary concerns to emerge from the 1-1 draw.

Mason Mount was forced off with an injury scare barely 20 minutes into the friendly after being named in Michael Carrick’s starting XI.

The former Chelsea star trudged from the field before holding a lengthy conversation with members of United’s medical staff and eventually heading down the tunnel.

It was another worrying sight for the injury-plagued midfielder, whose Old Trafford career has been repeatedly interrupted by fitness problems since his £60million move from Chelsea in 2023.

Young defender Ayden Heaven also found himself at the centre of controversy following a reckless challenge on PSG winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

The chaotic afternoon eventually finished 1-1 as United continued their preparations for the new campaign – but Carrick will be hoping his growing list of fitness concerns does not overshadow the rest of pre-season.

Sports.title: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick gives Mason Mount update and breaks silence on Marcus Rashford return
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK has downplayed concerns over Manchester United midfielder Mason Mount’s latest injury.

Mount was substituted after 20 minutes in United‘s 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg but jogged off the pitch.



The 27-year-old was walking freely when he made his way to the team coach after United’s fourth pre-season friendly and Carrick confirmed his withdrawal was a precaution.

“He got kicked,” Carrick said. “We just wanted to be careful and look after him.



“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”

Mount has played 72 times in three years for United, averaging only 24 appearances per season.

The former Chelsea player has been used in central midfield by Carrick during pre-season after he ended last season in a deeper role.

United are still lacking an available defensive midfielder, despite bolstering the area with summer signings Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

Carrick also confirmed Marcus Rashford’s imminent reunion with United after an 18-month absence from the first team squad.

Rashford is scheduled to travel to Dublin for United’s training camp that coincides with their penultimate friendly against Leeds United at Croke Park.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Barcelona passed on the option to sign Rashford for £26million and the England international is United’s highest earner on £325,000 a week.

Rashford has not played for United since a Europa League tie away to Viktoria Plzen in December 12 2024 and has spent spells on loan at Barca and Aston Villa, but he could be in line for a return for his parent club.

Carrick was the United captain when Rashford made his debut against Midtjylland in February 2016 and also coached and managed the 28-year-old.

“I’ve played with him,” Carrick added. “I played in the game he made his debut, so we have a history.

“We have a full squad next week in Dublin. We fly straight there and meet Leeds on Wednesday.



“We have a few days in Dublin where we have the whole squad, including Marcus, Kobbie (Mainoo) and Lisandro (Martinez).”

Sports.content:
Michael Carrick hails Man Utd quality 'people don't always see' after PSG fightback

Michael Carrick watched on as his Manchester United team recovered from conceding early against PSG to register a draw against the European champions

View 2 Images Man Utd secured a credible draw against PSG

Michael Carrick hailed his Manchester United side after their draw with PSG - insisting the players were able to find solutions throughout the game.

‌



The Red Devils took on the back-to-back Champions League winners in Sweden and fell behind inside two minutes despite Luis Enrique leaving out a lot of his frontline players.

‌



Bryan Mbeumo was able to equalise before half-time and it was the Premier League side who finished the stronger and can feel frustrated they didn't secure a statement pre-season victory.

‌



Carrick admits he and his coaching staff don't want to constantly solve problems for the players during the game, instead seeing if they can find the answers whilst on the pitch, which he's adamant will stand them in good stead for the upcoming season.

Sports.title: Arsenal line up £85m Vinicius Jr alternative but immediately hit by transfer issue
Sports.content:
Arsenal line up £85m Vinicius Jr alternative but immediately hit by transfer issue

Arsenal have missed out on landing a blockbuster move for Vinicius Junior, who will remain at Real Madrid, with their attention now turning to Kenan Yildiz at Juventus

View 2 Images Juventus' Kenan Yildiz is on Arsenal's radar

Arsenal are once again eyeing up a move for Juventus winger Kenan Yildiz after seeing their ambitious bid to lure Vinicius Junior to the Premier League fall flat.

‌



The Gunners had been eyeing a club-record move for the Real Madrid star, but the Brazilian has chosen to stay and extend his contract with Los Blancos, forcing the Premier League champions to look elsewhere.

‌



Arsenal are in the market for more firepower and are now said to have turned back to Yildiz, according to The Times. The north Londoners failed with an initial enquiry for Yildiz earlier this summer, while the Gunners also considered a move for the attacker 12 months ago. Juventus previously made it clear they wanted £85million for his services.

‌



Mikel Arteta has reignited his interest and reportedly reviewed the situation back in June, but the Serie A club made it clear that they do not want to sell the Turkey international - leaving Arsenal will another transfer fight on their hands.

Bruno Guimaraes reveals private Declan Rice message after sealing Arsenal transfer READ MORE :

Gabriel Jesus' agent addresses Arsenal transfer exit after being spotted at rival club READ MORE :

Juventus are ultimately in no hurry to sell and have the 21-year-old tied down on a contract until 2030, which he only signed in February. Yildiz scored 11 times in 47 outings last term and his displays saw him named the Serie A Rising Star of the Season.

The winger made three appearances for Turkey at the World Cup this summer but his preparations for the tournament were disrupted by a calf injury.

‌



Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti has come out this week and underlined his importance to the team as they look to ease him back to full fitness. "He is a very important footballer for us," he said. "For this reason, we are carefully managing his playing time, trying to build a correct schedule and work path to have him at his best throughout the season. But the fact that he is no longer in pain, that he is smiling and free to express his football is what makes us most happy."

View 2 Images Arsenal have missed out on Vinicius Jr (Image: (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images))

Arteta has already strengthened the left side of his attack by bringing in Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge for £34m. He compliments the squad's other wingers, which includes the likes of Gabriel Martinelli, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke.

Article continues below

Arsenal have also added proven Premier League quality in Bruno Guimaraes, who joined from Newcastle this weekend in a deal worth £75m. Another blockbuster deal during this window could take the club's expenditure past the £200m mark.

Sports.title: FIFA urged to change rule after 'criminal tackle' leaves star with shattered knee in pre-season
Sports.content:
FIFA urged to change rule after 'criminal tackle' leaves star with shattered knee in pre-season

Football clubs across Europe are in the middle of their pre-season preparations, and will be eager to keep their players fit and fresh for the new campaign

View Image Christantus Uche will miss the season through injury (Image: Getafe CF / X)

FIFA have been urged to change the rules surrounding red cards after a 'criminal tackle' which cut short Christantus Uche's season before it had even begun. Monaco ran out 1-0 winners of Getafe in a pre-season fixture at the Stade Louis-II on Thursday, Paris Brunner making the difference from the penalty spot in the second-half.

‌



However, what was meant to be a friendly quickly turned cynical for one pair of players, with Getafe's Uche left with a devastating knee injury following a late challenge from Christian Mawissa. Uche was left in a heap and in need of treatment when the Monaco defender caught him late with a lunging challenge.

‌



Uche's knee looked to be hyperextended as Mawissa caught him studs up on the shin, before flipping over onto his back, writhing in pain. Medical assistants were quickly called onto the pitch to give Uche treatment, as Mawissa was shown a straight red card.

‌



Violent brawl breaks out between fans in EFL Cup clash as police rush to intervene READ MORE :

Argentina at odds with England as statement released on FIFA president Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

Uche was ultimately taken off the pitch, unable to continue, with Getafe confirming the worst shortly afterward. While initial examinations pointed toward a contusion on Uche's kneecap, further tests revealed that not only was the 23-year-old forward's knee dislocated, but also in need of surgery after sustaining a number of torn ligaments.

It means that Uche is expected to miss the entirety of the upcoming La Liga season with Getafe, who will now have to scour the market to search for a late replacement. While Mawissa was rightly sent off for the challenge, a number of social media users were quick to call on FIFA to make changes to their rules surrounding red cards.

One wrote: "According to various newspapers, Uche will miss the entire season with Getafe due to this criminal tackle by Mawissa (Monaco) in a friendly match. His knee is shattered. Mawissa shouldn't play until Uche has recovered."

‌



A second, meanwhile, added: "It should be a FIFA rule. Whoever injures another player with a reckless or excessively forceful tackle shall be suspended from all competitions until the injured player returns to play, and during that time, they will earn the minimum salary of their league. THIS is how these absurd tackles would end."

A fourth suggested: "Monaco should pay for all of Uche's rehabilitation and charge it to Mawissa. Things like this should be severely punished, even if it was unintentional."

Meanwhile, a fifth explained: "When are they going to drop this proportionality between the challenge, the injury, and the sanction, but with the latter on a one-to-one basis, sanctioned and sidelined from playing until the injured player returns? Enough already with the overly lenient ones; you'd see how they'd think twice about those wildly disproportionate challenges."

We never want to see this kind of thing happen on the pitch. I wish him a speedy recovery and hope he can return as soon as possible."

Sports.title: Man Utd stars give Michael Carrick food for thought in PSG draw as transfer dilemma grows
Sports.content:
Man Utd stars give Michael Carrick food for thought in PSG draw as transfer dilemma grows

PSG 1-1 MANCHESTER UNITED: Bryan Mbuemo's first-half strike ensured the Premier League side held their own against the champions of Europe

View 3 Images Bryan Mbuemo impressed as Man Utd fought back against PSG

Talk of Marcus Rashford's possible return to the Manchester United fold has dominated the summer, but some of his team-mates showed that he's a way to go before he can start thinking of playing in red once more.

Rashford is back at Old Trafford following the end of his Barcelona loan and, with Ruben Amorim now gone, Michael Carrick could offer him fresh hope. Two of the immediate problems to Rashford's starting XI ambitions are Bryan Mbeumo and Amad.

Mbeumo was on target in their draw with PSG and was a constant menace for the Red Devils. On one of the flanks was Amad, who dovetailed impressively with the Cameroonian.

United responded well to an early onslaught, that saw PSG teenager Ibrahim Mbaye open the scoring inside two minutes at the back post. Mbeumo had the Premier League side level before half-time as he finished neatly after Amad had set him away.

Mason Mount forced off through injury as Man Utd suffer blow in PSG friendly READ MORE :

Ex-Man Utd title winner back in England looking for new club as a free agent READ MORE :

Patrick Dorgu was another element of the United attack. Signed by Amorim as a wing-back, the return to a more conventional formation may have left him wondering where his future lied in the team. Carrick is understood to prefer him in a more advanced role, giving Rashford yet more competition.

Dorgu also has the added luxury of having a body of work under Carrick, which the United boss will no doubt factor in to his selection decisions. Rashford was afforded an extended break having been involved with England at the World Cup, but that may well have him on the back foot.

This was a United XI that left Bruno Fernandes on the bench initially, has Benjamin Sesko still recovering from injury and Matheus Cunha still to come back into the picture.

View 3 Images Amad began out wide and impressed with Patrick Dorgu and Shea Lacey also being used on the wings

Youngster Shea Lacey moved out to the left once Fernandes came on to occupy his usual role as the team's playmaker, meaning the teenager is another player Carrick wants to look at in one of the wide roles. This United depth is starting to look more and more impressive, even if Rashford's task is being made all the more challenging.

The Englishman is still United's top earner and, if he is going to play a squad role, then the club may have to look at moving him on. His salary will make that a challenge, but the club can ill-afford to pay someone who pops off the bench more than £300,000-a-week.

This was a game that showed United, who still have questions to answer given the impact of the well renowned 'new manager bounce', can at least mix it in the pre-season environment with PSG.

The French champions were certainly showcasing their depth and sone of the next generation. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Willian Pacho were the only two men to start in the Champions League final that began from the off in Sweden.

View 3 Images Shea Lacey is looking to stake his claim to become a regular

It means it was not the type of Parisian test that Arsenal faced when they tried to beat them to win the European Cup, but it was still a well coached side that began flexing their muscles on the hour mark. Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes, Vitinha and Joao Neves all came on once the hour mark hit.

United sent on summer signing Youri Tielemans in the second-half and the Belgian quickly set about trying to conduct proceedings. He found Fernandes with a neat ball, but his effort in the final ten minutes went wide.

Article continues below

It was actually United who had the better of the final stages, but they were unable to find the winner that would've landed them a morale-boosting scalp, even if this was a PSG side not a full strength.

Sports.title: Mason Mount forced off through injury as Man Utd suffer blow in PSG friendly
Sports.content:
Mason Mount forced off through injury as Man Utd suffer blow in PSG friendly

Mason Mount went off injured in the 20th minute of Manchester United's pre-season friendly against Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg on Saturday

View 2 Images Mason Mount went off injured against PSG (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has been handed an injury concern ahead of the start of the season after being forced to substitute Mason Mount against Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



Mount has been a bright spark for United during their pre-season friendlies so far. But the midfielder had to leave the pitch in Gothenburg on Saturday afternoon in the 20th minute against PSG, with Tyler Fletcher replacing him.

‌



He was able to jog off the pitch before speaking to the United medical staff on the touchline. The severity of the injury was unclear and it could just prove to be a precautionary move. Things went from bad to worse in the second half when veteran goalkeeper Tom Heaton was replaced by Dermot Mee following what appeared to be a hamstring injury.

‌



The 27-year-old has failed to live up to his £55million price tag since arriving in the summer of 2023, with injuries hampering his efforts. The former Chelsea man has started just 25 Premier League matches in three seasons for United.

He left the pitch due to some discomfort on Saturday, with Carrick taking no chances. Mount will be assessed, but Carrick may well be worried given his injury history and the proximity to the start of the 2026/27 season. United kick-off their campaign against newly-promoted Hull City on August 22.

‌



They were 1-0 down when Mount departed the pitch, having conceded a goal to Ibrahim Mbaye in the second minute of the match. Bryan Mbeumo made it 1-1 in the 32nd minute with a low finish into the bottom corner after good work from Amad Diallo.

United have lost 1-0 to Wrexham, beaten Rosenborg 5-0 and overcome Atletico Madrid 2-1 in their pre-season friendlies so far. After playing PSG in Sweden this weekend, they head to Ireland to face Leeds on Wednesday night and to Poland to play AC Milan in Wroclaw next Saturday.

View 2 Images Bryan Mbuemo equalised for Manchester United against PSG (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



While some of United's players have returned late to Carrick's squad following involvement in the World Cup, Mount has made the most of the time. He has been one of the stand-out players in the friendlies and will be hoping to force his way into the starting line-up come the start of the season.

There will be plenty of competition for places. United have spent a combined £87million to sign Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa this summer to bolster their options in central midfield.

Mount took the captain's armband in Norway and has been looking forward to playing a leadership role this season. "You have different types of leaders," he said recently. "You have ones that are very vocal, but I see myself as one who leads by example and never stops working. I've been captain previously, years ago, so I love the role.

Article continues below

"Especially with a lot of younger players on the pitch, and off it as well, being able to speak to them and make them feel comfortable, it's something I really like."

Sports.title: Darwin Nunez has given thumbs up to Liverpool transfer as deal gets seal of approval
Sports.content:
Darwin Nunez has given thumbs up to Liverpool transfer as deal gets seal of approval

Former Liverpool striker Darwin Nunez has already shared his thoughts on Ronald Araujo, who is set to join the club from Barcelona

View 2 Images Darwin Nunez has previously discussed his Uruguay teammate Ronald Araujo (Image: Luis ROBAYO / AFP via Getty Images)

Former Liverpool star Darwin Nunez has already lauded Ronald Araujo's key traits as the defender edges closer to a move to Anfield. The Reds have pursued the Barcelona star to shore up their defensive concerns.

‌



Araujo is on the verge of completing a loan move from Barcelona to strengthen Liverpool's backline. Andoni Iraola's side need more options in defence, with skipper Virgil van Dijk currently the only senior centre-back available to the manager.

‌



Araujo predominantly operates as a central defender but can also fill in at right-back, addressing issues in two positions. The Liverpool ECHO has reported that the loan deal includes a buy option, with the defender due to undergo a medical on Sunday.

‌



The 27-year-old featured in Uruguay's World Cup squad this summer, although he remained on the sidelines due to a calf problem. Former Liverpool striker Nunez is a friend of Araujo's and has previously spoken glowingly of the defender's character off the pitch.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Ronald, well, he's been my friend for a long time," Nunez told AUFTV in May 2025. "He's a very humble person, he comes from the same background as me, he also has the same characteristics as me, we both come from towns that are very far from the city of Montevideo."

‌



Beyond their close friendship, Nunez highlighted the qualities that best define Araujo: "This is a humble person, a cheerful person, a family man and a good friend."

Nunez would likely be delighted that Liverpool are opting to sign Araujo. The striker also demonstrated his fondness for the defender in 2022, when Araujo's prospects of featuring at the World Cup appeared uncertain.

Sports.title: Cristian Romero faces furious backlash as Tottenham captain 'wants Arsenal transfer'
Sports.content:
Cristian Romero faces furious backlash as Tottenham captain 'wants Arsenal transfer'

Cristian Romero is expected to leave Tottenham this summer and whilst Arsenal are interested in the central defender their arch-rivals will not entertain the prospect of a move

View 2 Images Cristian Romero is tipped to leave Tottenham this summer (Image: Alex Pantling, Getty Images)

Cristian Romero is open to joining Arsenal this summer - but Tottenham are adamant their defender will not be crossing the north London divide.

‌



The Argentine wants to call time on his five year spell with Tottenham and there is interest from Atletico Madrid and Inter Milan, but the Gunners too are keen on the centre-half in a move which would spark a furious backlash from Spurs fans.

‌



Despite Romero's stance on the move, Tottenham bosses have made it clear that there is no scenario where they will allow their defender to move to the Emirates, claims The Sun.

‌



A transfer would see Romero emulate Sol Campbell's move from Tottenham to Arsenal in 2001, which remains one of the most controversial transfers in the history of the Premier League. Campbell was a leading light at White Hart Lane but chose to leave when his contract expired, which effectively left Tottenham powerless to prevent the move.

Bruno Guimaraes reveals private Declan Rice message after sealing Arsenal transfer READ MORE :

Four left-backs Man Utd can sign after Newcastle block Lewis Hall transfer move READ MORE :

However Romero still has a contract at Tottenham, which has three years left to run, and that puts his club in a strong position when it comes to his future. The 28-year-old's departure is expected but the north Londoners will not be letting him make the 4.5 mile trip to their rivals.

William Gallas was the last man to make the switch, that coming in 2010, but like Campbell his move came upon the expiry of his contract rather than the two clubs actually coming to the negotiation table.

‌



Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi has already signed Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton for £52million with the Dutchman effectively serving a Romero's replacement. Van Hecke is part of a summer spree that has seen the club spend over £200m on new talent, which includes Sandro Tonali.

View 2 Images Sol Campbell caused uproar when moving from Tottenham to Arsenal (Image: Jamie McDonald/ALLSPORT)

Atletico have a long-term interest in Romero and any move to the Spanish capital would allow him to work under Diego Simeone, who is known to be a huge fan of his fellow Argentina. He is thought to be readying a £40m bid for Romero.

‌



The La Liga side tried to sign Romero last summer, but former Tottenham boss Thomas Frank convinced the defender to sign a new deal and made him the club captain.

Romero was heavily criticised when it emerged that he was going to miss Tottenham's must win final game of last season. He headed back to Argentina to watch boyhood club Belgrano face River Plate in a title decider, but made a late u-turn and was present for the win over Everton.

Sports.title: Wissa double gives Newcastle boss Jaissle winning start at 10-man Valencia
Sports.content:
Substitute Yoane Wissa scored twice to give Matthias Jaissle a winning start as Newcastle boss with a 2-1 comeback pre-season win at 10-man Valencia.

But the friendly at the Mestalla threatened to be overshadowed by Jose Gaya's red-card horror tackle on Anthony Elanga, which saw the Newcastle winger stretchered off in the first half and led to both sets of players clashing.

Fortunately for the Sweden international, his injury does not appear to be serious, with Elanga later up and walking after a contusion to the shin.



Image: Tempers flared after Jose Gaya's challenge saw Anthony Elanga stretchered off

A stunning fifth-minute opener from Valencia's Filip Ugrinic and then Elanga's injury gave Jaissle a nightmare start to life in the Newcastle dugout.

But his half-time changes sparked a Toon turnaround with new signings Bazoumana Toure and Sean Steur impressing.

It was last summer's signing Wissa who pounced on a mistake to level in the 52nd minute.

New arrival Toure then broke clear of the Valencia defence to unselfishly set up Wissa for a tap-in to complete the comeback in the 76th minute.

Toure should have had a second assist after fine work down the left, but Jacob Murphy put over his cross in stoppage time.

The win brings some relief to Newcastle on the day they lost their captain Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal.

Jaissle's next pre-season test will come on Wednesday as his new side face Everton at Murrayfield in Edinburgh.

Sports.title: 'Good signs' for Man Utd as Mbeumo scores in encouraging  draw with PSG
Sports.content:
Bryan Mbeumo earned Man Utd a 1-1 draw with Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg, a pre-season friendly which left boss Michael Carrick encouraged by the "good signs" from his side.

A slow start, which saw Liverpool-linked Ibrahim Mbaye tuck in a PSG opener after just two minutes and the European champions - despite missing many of their star names - stretch United, was overcome and fears of an injury to Mason Mount were also allayed, with the midfielder later seen walking freely after being forced off during the first half.

The standout Amad Diallo was key to United shifting the momentum. He won the ball back high up the pitch to tee up Mbeumo for a fine finish for United's equaliser and proved too hot to handle for the PSG defence into the half-time break.

Mbeumo would have added to his tally had PSG's Matvey Safonov not been in such sharp form, although the goalkeeper left the pitch to jeers after escaping punishment for clattering Joshua Zirkzee way outside of his area.

Image: Youri Tielemans made his first appearance for Man Utd against PSG

At the other end, United goalkeeper Tom Heaton suffered a hamstring issue and had to be replaced. It was a problem which appears more significant than the injury Mount seemingly got to his left foot, which Carrick later suggested was just a kick. With Altay Bayindir loaned to Celta Vigo and Radek Vitek sold to Middlesbrough, 23-year-old Dermot Mee came on for his debut.

There were late chances for Tyler Fletcher, Shea Lacey and captain Bruno Fernandes - who linked up excitingly with new signing Youri Tielemans. United weren't able to find a winner but this was a performance to be positive about.

Man Utd team news: Tielemans on for debut as Bruno returns Youri Tielemans came on as a second-half sub to make his Man Utd debut in Sweden. Captain Bruno Fernandes also entered the action for his first minutes of pre-season.



Michael Carrick had made just one change from the side which started the win over Atletico Madrid last weekend, with Noussair Mazraoui coming in for Leny Yoro.



PSG were without their France stars Ousmane Dembele, Desire Doue or Bradley Barcola.

The key moments from Gothenberg...

2: GOAL! Ibrahim Mbaye tucks in the opener at the back post from Dro Fernandez's cross after Ayden Heaven is unable to cut it out.

4: SHOT! PSG threaten again with Khvicha Kvaratskhelia denied from distance by Tom Heaton.

16: BLOCK! Andrey Santos slides in to block Mbaye's shot over the bar with United stretched.

20: INJURY! Mason Mount is forced off injured with an apparent foot injury.

32: GOAL! Amad Diallo wins the ball back high up the pitch and feeds Bryan Mbeumo who cracks an equaliser across goal and into the bottom corner.

Man Utd on the front foot Man Utd had 24 touches in the opposition box. PSG managed just seven.

36: NO PENALTY! Amad's appeals are waved away when Willian Pacho nudges him as he goes for a header.

38: SAVE! For the second time in the match Mbeumo tests PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov with a free-kick shot.

48: INJURY! Heaton injures his right hamstring making a clearance and Dermot Mee comes on in his place.

54: SAVE! Stunning stop from Safonov to deny Mbeumo's shot towards the top corner from outside the box.

72: DRAMA! Safonov rushes out of his box and clatters Zirkzee with his shoulder as United try to counter no foul is given and after Jack Fletcher declines a long-range shot at the unguarded goal, Shea Lacey's effort is blocked behind.

87: CHANCES! Dalot's cross is met by Tyler Fletcher but he twice has efforts blocked before Lacey lashes over from a tight angle

89: CLOSE! Fernandes whips a shot just wide of the far post with a bouncing shot from outside the box.

Carrick 'enjoyed' PSG draw: 'We should have scored more goals'

Man Utd head coach Michael Carrick to MUTV:

"I enjoyed it. Good challenge. Slightly different with the way they play. We should've scored more goals.

"Very different to what we've played against, the boys adapted really well, so there were a lot of positives from the game. The things we were trying to get out of the game, a lot of it was there.

"It's good for the boys sometimes to have to problem solve and find their own way and I thought we did that. That prepares them for the season as well. In that respect there were a lot of things that maybe people don't always see that we were quite happy with. There were some good signs there."

Attacking positives for Man Utd in PSG draw

Sky Sports' Peter Smith:

"Man Utd's attack caught the eye on Saturday, with Bryan Mbeumo and Amad Diallo looking sharp and the connection between Youri Tielemans and Bruno Fernandes already clicking.

"Amad played a big part in shifting the momentum United's way after PSG's fast start. In the final third he won the ball back and passed it more than any other player on the pitch.

"That impact with and without the ball was clear when he found Mbeumo for the equaliser - and the striker's finish was excellent.

"Mbeumo could easily have scored more but for some good goalkeeping, landing four shots on target. No other player managed more than one.

"Debutant Tielemans and returning captain Fernandes could not be expected to be so sharp making their first minutes of pre-season - but still they produced some nice link-up play and signs they will be a big influence in this coming campaign.

"Tielemans' passing from deep was classy; Fernandes was immediately a threat around the edge of the box.

"As Michael Carrick said afterwards, 'good signs' for the season ahead."

Sports.title: Walsh battles through cuts and knockdown to drop Denny and take victory
Sports.content:
Callum Walsh maintained his unbeaten record and top contender status with a unanimous decision victory over Tyler Denny.

Denny, a former European champion, is a tough veteran and proved a test for the Irish middleweight at Dublin's 3Arena.

Walsh prevailed on points, winning 98-91 twice and 96-90.

The bout didn't progress without its pitfalls as Denny gave him hard rounds.

The first round suddenly went south for Walsh. Awkwardly positioned in front of Denny, he found himself bending low. Denny attacked and Walsh took a shot before slipping to a knee. The referee ruled that a knockdown.

Image: Walsh has a knockdown scored against him.

Walsh found the perfect riposte in the second round. As Denny came after him, Walsh launched a lovely arching left cross to the point of the Englishman's chin, dropping him heavily to the canvas.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Callum Walsh put Tyler Denny down in the second round with a huge left hand punch.

Denny, brave as ever, rose and fought on. But Walsh popped up from beneath an attack to land a fine right hook and he finished the round slugging Denny into the ropes.

The Briton shook off the effects of that round and advanced. By the end of the fourth round, Walsh was backing up, letting his southpaw opponent come on but picking out accurate punches to catch Denny.

Walsh maintained his control, moving, hitting and letting Denny work to try to pin him down.

The Briton kept scrapping forward and managed to land solidly in the sixth round.

Denny trudged on swinging wildly, but Walsh manoeuvred well. The Irishman caught Denny to the head with a left-right combination. Denny felt those shots but remained doggedly determined. He cleaved away with uppercuts in close.

Image: Walsh readies to uncork his southpaw left

The referee took a point off Walsh for holding, before evening up it by taking a point off Denny for hitting behind the head.

Walsh exploded forward with a savage sequence of punches to the head, leaving Denny stranded, standing still on the end of them.

But Walsh emerged from a clash with a cut over his left eye. It bled badly at once. Denny was leaning into him in scrappy collisions and Walsh looked frustrated after picking an additional nick on his cheek.

In the 10th round Walsh landed a great lead right uppercut. Denny got after him with hooks, catching the Irishman with his southpaw left and right.

Another hard left from Walsh though snagged Denny. He couldn't put the Englishman down a second time but made sure he finished the fight in the ascendancy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights of Callum Walsh's clash with Tyler Denny from Zuffa Boxing 10 in Dublin.

'I think he broke my orbital bone'

Walsh told Sky Sports: "It was a lot harder than I thought. In the second round we clashed heads. I think he broke my orbital bone. It was crunching the whole time.

"It was very tough. I'm very critical of myself. I should have been a lot better. I wish I could have been better.

"He's tough, awkward and tricky, but we'll go again."
