Sports.title: Joao Palhinha in talks over return to the Premier League after Tottenham exit
Sports.content:
Joao Palhinha in talks over return to the Premier League after Tottenham exit

Aston Villa are in talks over a deal for Joao Palhinha, their director of football has confirmed.

The midfielder is one of three players that Bayern Munich are willing to sell this summer.

2 Palhinha could be set for another season in the Premier League at a new club Credit: Getty

Palhinha joined Bayern from Fulham in 2024 and he spent last season on loan at Tottenham Hotspur.

His move to north London included a £26million option to buy, but it expired and he has returned to Germany.

With the Portuguese international not in Bayern's plans, he looks set to leave just two seasons after he signed.

A return to the Premier League appears to be on the cards as Damian Vidagany told BILD that Villa are working on a move.

"We need a midfielder because Amadou Onana is out for the entire season - Joao Palhinha is a very good player who would fit our plans," Vidagany said.

"We are in talks, but there is currently no agreement. I believe Aston Villa would be a great club for him."

That was as much as Vidagany was willing to give away, as he refused to comment on further details due to the 'great respect' all at Villa have for Bayern.

Palhinha has made 101 appearances in the Premier League across his stints at Fulham and Spurs.

A move to Villa would present him with an opportunity to play in the Champions League during the new season.

Newcastle United, who have lost Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal, have also been linked with Palhinha.

Midfield moves

2 Palhinha impressed at Spurs, but they chose not to pursue a permanent deal Credit: Getty

Villa have already completed two signings in central midfield so far this summer.

Johan Manzambi was brought in from SC Freiburg in a £52million deal that made him their club-record signing.

Villa have also signed Joao Gomes from West Midlands rivals Wolves for £35m.

Ross Barkley, John McGinn, Boubacar Kamara and Lamare Bogarde are listed as central midfielders on Villa's website.

However, Youri Tielemans has departed for Manchester United, whilst Enzo Barrenechea is back at Benfica after a loan spell.

Villa begin their season on Wednesday night when they take on Paris Saint-Germain in the Super Cup, live on talkSPORT.

Their first Premier League fixture comes four days later on August 23 with a trip to Brighton.

Sports.title: New EFL signing immediately forced to clarify ‘stepping stone’ comment amid backlash
Sports.content:
Middlesbrough signing Radek Vitek has been forced to explain a comment made during his first interview after his transfer.

Vitek signed for Boro from Manchester United on Saturday, but he said that the move was a 'new stepping stone' for him.



2 New Middlesbrough goalkeeper Vitek received backlash for his first interview Credit: Getty

His wording led to some backlash from fans online, as they questioned his mentality regarding the switch.

Typically, the phrase 'a stepping stone' relates to a player using a smaller club solely as a route to join a bigger team in the future, rather than planning to stay for a long time.

After Middlesbrough posted a video of Vitek's first interview as their new signing, supporters flooded the replies.



One Boro supporter replied on X: "Don’t love how he has just called us a stepping stone."

Another questioned: "Did he just say stepping stone..."

"Lad really said ‘new stepping stone’ Jesus. Welcome to the club, I guess," a third Boro fan posted.



But some fans jumped to Vitek's defence and pointed out a language barrier that could have impacted the Czech star.

"I think he means 'next step in my career' having listened to it a few times," another Middlesbrough supporter said. "Easy to mix up sayings when it's someone's second language."



'Not meant in any negative way'

And just a few hours after Vitek's first interview was posted and he faced some backlash, he spoke out on the matter.

"I wanted to clarify what I meant by 'stepping stone'," the goalkeeper wrote, explaining his words on his X account.

What did Radek Vitek say in his interview? In the video posted by Middlesbrough on Saturday, Vitek could be heard saying: "A new challenge for me. "A new stepping stone in my career, a permanent move. "So I'm really excited. I hope everyone is as excited as me for the season ahead and I hope we can go for the goal we all want."

"I just want to assure everyone that I have not meant that in any negative way.

"The point of this comment was that this is a very important step in my career going forward.



"I can’t wait to get started."

Off to a controversial start

Vitek won't have wanted any controversy to begin his time as a Middlesbrough player, but he has now cleared things up.

The 22-year-old has joined the club from Man United after spending the last six years with the Red Devils.

He spent last season on loan at Bristol City in the Championship, following other loans in the EFL and Austria.

2 Vitek spent pre-season with Man United after a loan at Bristol City last term Credit: Getty



Vitek was named Bristol City's Player of the Year after an impressive campaign - and now he's back in the second tier.

Away from his 'stepping stone' comments in his first interview as a Boro player, he also said: “It feels great to be here.

“This is a new challenge for me and I’m really excited to be a Boro player.

“The project here is very impressive, because you can clearly see the ambition and where the club wants to go.



“I’m delighted to now be part of that.”

Sports.title: South Korean FA apologises after headquarters raided over sexual services for refs allegations
Sports.content:
South Korean FA apologises after headquarters raided over sexual services for refs allegations

South Korea’s FA has issued an apology following reports that it had provided 'sexual services' to foreign referees.

The country’s broadcaster JTBC reported earlier this week that the Korea Football Association (KFA) had offered the services to officials that were in the country for international matches.



3 The South Korean FA is under the microscope yet again Credit: AFP

The allegations date back more than a decade ago with referees offered services on multiple occasions in 2011 and 2012.

It is alleged that further indiscretions occurred prior to qualifying matches for the 2014 World Cup and the 2012 London Olympics.

In a statement, the KFA profusely apologised for the details of the report.



KFA's statement on shock allegations

It read: “We deeply apologise for causing concern over various issues involving the association, which emerged from a parliamentary hearing and an unprecedented search and seizure, and from reports about events from more than a decade ago, that even many within the organisation were unaware of.'”

The news report published on Thursday revealed how a sports ministry investigation back in 2016 found the KFA had provided inappropriate entertainment to foreign referees.



It claimed that it happened on seven separate occasions between March 2011 and March 2012.

The services included trips to massage parlours with the fees inclusive of the costs of sexual services.



“The association makes clear that inappropriate conduct of this kind, or the use of corporate cards for such purposes, is absolutely not currently taking place,” the KFA added in its statement.

The allegations come after a period of instability on and off the pitch in South Korean football.

A review into an issue involving the appointment of former national team coach Hong Myung-bo is ongoing.

3 Hong Myung-bo's appointment as South Korea head coach is under investigation



Seoul police raided the KFA’s offices on Thursday as part of their inquiries into Hong’s selection.

The investigation began shortly after Hong’s appointment but to a halt this summer after nearly two years without answers.

However, public anger surrounding South Korea’s disappointing World Cup group-stage exit brought about renewed attention.

Ex-KFA technical director Lee Lim-saeng is accused of offering Hong the job at a bakery near the coach’s home.



South Korea’s sports ministry said in 2024 that Lee’s meeting with Hong was not a formal interview and that the KFA had breached its own hiring rules.

However, the ministry found no evidence of foul play.

3 South Korea endured a hugely disappointing World Cup campaign this summer Credit: AFP

“When I received the offer, I thought they had all taken the proper steps,” Hong said at the parliamentary hearing.

“People may think things were not so transparent, but I never once asked for any special treatment.”

Sports.title: Mason Mount sparks new injury fears by limping out of Man United pre-season game
Sports.content:
Mason Mount sparks new injury fears by limping out of Man United pre-season game

Mason Mount was forced off with an injury scare during Manchester United's pre-season clash with Paris Saint-Germain.

The 27-year-old has been blighted by fitness issues since his move to Old Trafford in 2023, but was named in Michael Carrick's starting XI as they took on the European champions in Gothenburg.

4 Mount was in conversation with Man United's medical team after lasting less than 20 minutes against PSG Credit: X: @samuelluckhurst

4 The Englishman headed straight down the tunnel after his afternoon was cut short Credit: X: @samuelluckhurst

But there was no let-up for Mount in the pre-season fixture, as he pulled up early on and was unable to continue.

The 27-year-old then had to be replaced by Tyler Fletcher in yet more concerning scenes.

After exiting the field, Mount could be seen deep in conversation with members of United’s medical staff.

He then made his way down the tunnel, in a familiar sight for Red Devils supporters.

Man United were 1-0 down to a youthful PSG side when Mount was forced off, with Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye putting the Champions League winners in front within two minutes.

But Carrick's side responded soon after, as Bryan Mbeumo equalised shortly after the half-hour mark.

In the wars

Injuries have plagued Mount's Man United career, preventing him from reaching the standards he set at previous club Chelsea.

The Cobham academy graduate joined the Red Devils in a £60million deal in 2023.

However, since then he has spent a staggering 394 days on the sidelines, causing him to miss both Euro 2024 and this summer's World Cup with England.

Mount has made just 72 appearances for United, but made his most appearances in a Premier League campaign for the club last term.

4 Mount was in Sweden for Man Utd’s latest pre-season clash Credit: Getty

The England midfielder featured 23 times in the league, scoring three goals, although he was mainly used by former boss Ruben Amorim in the first half of the season.

This has led to rumours he could join Amorim at new club AC Milan, although Mount has been part of United's pre-season group so far.

Make or break?

Mount's latest setback against PSG come after talkSPORT's Shebahn Aherne suggested that the upcoming season was make-or-break for him in his career.

“He needs to have a strong season,” Aherne said of Mount.

“Luke Shaw played every game last season and really got his season back on track, sorted out the injury issues and he was brilliant.

“But Mason Mount, you always hear that he’s the perfect pupil. He’s a very smart and intelligent player and when he’s on his game. He’s brilliant.

4 Mount has scored just seven goals in his injury-hit Man United career Credit: Getty

“You just hope that this season he will come good.”

talkSPORT's Tony Cascarino was also hopeful the 27-year-old could find his level again and highlighted one of his key attributes.

He said: “They paid £55m for him. He was injured at Chelsea before he got to Old Trafford and he was a terrific player for Chelsea.

“He can play in that floating position like [Florian] Wirtz and he can get a goal.

“Manchester United need a really fit Mason Mount, if not to start, then to challenge for other player’s spots in the team.

“He’s a good finisher, get him in goalscoring positions and he will finish. It would be like a new signing.”

Sports.title: West Ham and Tottenham agree £5m fee for Manor Solomon, Barcelona to table new bid for Man City's Rodri - and Southampton eye move for Man United youngster: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
West Ham and Tottenham agree £5m fee for Manor Solomon, Barcelona to table new bid for Man City's Rodri - and Southampton eye move for Man United youngster: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Everton target the Cherry on top

Everton have added Bournemouth winger Marcus Tavernier to their list of potential wing options this summer.

The 27-year-old is valued around £35m-£40m by Bournemouth.

Everton have also checked on Galatasaray's Baris Yilmaz and Crystal Palace's Brennan Johnson among others.

Everton and Palace discuss McNeil-Johnson swap

Everton and Crystal Palace are in discussions over a potential swap deal between Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson.

Everton and Crystal Palace are in discussions over a potential swap deal between Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson

McNeil was left upset after a move to Palace fell through in January while Johnson has been struggling to find his form since joining in a £35million deal from Tottenham also in the winter window.

The 25-year-old hasn't managed a single goal in his 18 appearances since joining the Eagles.

He has also failed to earn a starting berth, and a trial as a right-wing back under former manager Oliver Glasner failed to trigger improvement. However, David Moyes is a long-term admirer.

McNeil rediscovered form after February but wants more regular starts.

Solomon fee agreed

West Ham and Tottenham have agreed a deal for Manor Solomon at £5million plus add-ons for the 27-year-old winger.

He is expected to undergo his medical over the next 48 hours.

Loan star Ronald Araujo to check in at Liverpool

Ronald Araujo will have a medical at Liverpool on Sunday ahead of completing his loan with option to buy from Barcelona.

Ronald Araujo will have a medical at Liverpool on Sunday ahead of a loan with option to buy

The fee on the option to buy for the 27-year-old defender is £47million.

Araujo is preparing to travel to link up with Liverpool ahead of signing his contract and meeting his new teammates tomorrow.

The Uruguay international gives Liverpool experience and vital defensive cover as he is able to play at centre-back and right-back.

Araujo wanted to go because after talks with coach Hansi Flick it was apparent he would not be guaranteed regular starts and he believes he will find greater opportunity to do so under Andoni Iraola at Liverpool.

The Spanish champions are working to offload a number of players as they look to upgrade their squad. They are focused on signing Rodri from Manchester City and still want to strengthen their own centre-back options and at striker.

Araujo will say farewell to Barcelona teammates today prior to heading for Merseyside on Sunday.

Liverpool remain in talks for Paris Saint-Germain pair Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.

Full story

Forest on cusp of £36m Diomande move

Nottingham Forest are closing on a £36million deal for Sporting Lisbon centre-back Ousmane Diomande.

The proposed transfer looked to be off last week but a series of conversations have ironed out differences and the 22-year-old Ivory Coast international is due to travel over tomorrow ahead of undergoing a medical.

Forest have a five-year contract in place for the defender.

Forest centre-back Nikola Milenkovic is an option being considered by Juventus while Murillo also has interest from other clubs.

Nottingham Forest are closing on a £36m deal for Sporting centre back Ousmane Diomande

Barca set to table new Rodri bid

Barcelona are preparing a new bid for Manchester City midfielder Rodri after their initial £38million offer plus bonuses was dismissed.

City want £68million for the 30-year-old Spain captain.

Barca are looking to find moves for a number of players including Marc Casado, Roony Bardghji, Hector Fort, Alvaro Cortes, Tommy Marques, Ferran Torres, who is bound for Paris St Germain and Ronald Araujo who is off to Liverpool.

Hammers re-enter Solomon talks

West Ham have revived talks with Tottenham over a deal for winger Manor Solomon.

Talks initially broke down over bonuses due if West Ham were promoted which the Championship side thought were unreasonable but the clubs are working towards a £10million agreement.

Saints eye Man United youngster Kamason

Manchester United full-back Jaydan Kamason is wanted by Southampton.

The Championship side would like the 19-year-old England youth international on a permanent transfer and he is also receiving enquiries from others wanting him on loan.

Preston North End, Blackburn Rovers, Bristol City and Sheffield Wednesday have shown interest in the right-back while there are clubs abroad keen to take him.

Kamason though has a lot of admirers at Old Trafford. He was one of the academy players who excelled in the opening games of United's pre-season, particularly in the 5-0 win over Rosenborg.

He was the first player to sign scholarship forms at United after coming through the club's Emerging Talent Programme, which he joined at 10, while playing for grassroots team Stockport Vikings.

United have yet to decide on plans for his development but he looks likely to stay around Michael Carrick's squad until January.

Goalkeeper Radek Vítek has completed his move to Middlesbrough on a permanent transfer from United in a deal worth up to £14million.

Jaydan Kamason has excelled in pre-season games for United and has plenty of admirers

Geronimo Rulli medical at Man City

Marseille goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli is due to undergo a medical at Manchester City on Monday after the clubs agreed a £1.75million deal.

Rulli, who is set to sign a two-year deal at the Etihad, joins as a replacement for James Trafford, who completed a club-record move to Leeds for £45million.

Rulli has been identified by City as the man to provide backup to Gianluigi Donnarumma next season.

Atletico's Ruggeri to join Villa for £16million

Atletico Madrid left-back Matteo Ruggeri has agreed to join Aston Villa. The 24-year-old Italian will cost £16million plus add-ons.

His transfer will help pave the way for Atletico to bid for Tottenham captain Cristian Romero.

The Argentine centre-back is also among names being considered by Barcelona but Atletico coach Diego Simeone hopes to convince his compatriot if they can agree on terms.

Matteo Ruggeri's move should pave the way for Cristian Romero to join Atletico Madrid

Facundo Buonanotte leaves Brighton for Elche

Brighton midfielder Facundo Buonanotte has joined La Liga side Elche on a season-long loan.

The 21-year-old was on loan at two different Premier League clubs last season, spending the first half with Chelsea before joining Leeds in the second half of the campaign.

Sheffield Wednesday chase Liverpool star Scanlon

Liverpool left-back Calum Scanlon is wanted on loan by Sheffield Wednesday.

The 21-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at Cardiff City and they are keen to take him back too.

Scanlon has impressed on Liverpool's pre-season and is attracting a number of enquiries but League One Wednesday, who play Bolton in the Carabao Cup today, are making a concerted effort to take the England U20 international to Hillsborough.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick provides Mason Mount injury update after Man United star hobbled off just 20 minutes into pre-season draw against PSG - sparking fears over team's midfield options
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick provides Mason Mount injury update after Man United star hobbled off just 20 minutes into pre-season draw against PSG - sparking fears over team's midfield options

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Mason Mount was forced off with an injury during Manchester United's friendly against Paris Saint-Germain, although United boss Michael Carrick was quick to assuage any fears that it could be a long-term issue.

The 27-year-old midfielder has been one of United's standout performers in pre-season, but his latest appearance was cut short after he was substituted just 20 minutes into the match in Gothenburg and replaced by Tyler Fletcher.

Mount spoke to three members of the medical staff before heading down the tunnel and appeared to be experiencing a problem with his foot. He was able to jog off when his number was shown and was later moving well when heading to board the team bus, with Carrick confirming the move had been precautionary.

'He got kicked,' Carrick said after the final whistle. 'We just wanted to be careful and look after him. We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.'

Carrick's comments will come as a welcome boost for United ahead of the new season, which begins in two weeks time.

United, who qualified for the Champions League with their third-place finish last term, kick off their campaign away at newly-promoted Hull. They then host Ipswich and travel to Everton before Old Trafford stages the Manchester derby on September 13.

The midfielder has been one of United's standout performers in pre-season, but his latest appearance was cut short after he was substituted just 20 minutes into the match

Mount spoke to three members of the medical staff before heading down the tunnel and appeared to be experiencing a problem with his foot

Mount, who joined United from Chelsea in a £60million deal in 2023, has struggled with injuries during his time at the club, making 72 appearances across three seasons.

Of the three seasons he has been at United, he made the most top-flight appearances last term with 23, averaging just 44 minutes per game.

In Sweden, United drew 1-1 to United fell behind in the second minute when 18-year-old striker Ibrahim Mbaye buried his chance at the far post.

Bryan Mbeumo then levelled the scoring half an hour later. Amad Diallo won the ball and carried it forward before feeding Mbeumo to the left of the box, with the Cameroonian burying his shot into the far corner.

Neither side could find a winner after the break as the match finished 1-1.

Sports.title: Man United flop Antony is SENT OFF as pre-season friendly between Bournemouth and Real Betis descends into a brawl - with Cherries star also seeing red
Sports.content:
Man United flop Antony is SENT OFF as pre-season friendly between Bournemouth and Real Betis descends into a brawl - with Cherries star also seeing red

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Bournemouth's Alex Scott and former Man United winger Antony were shown red cards after a brawl during the Cherries' pre-season friendly with Real Betis.

Players from both sides clashed in the closing stages of the first half at the Benito Villamarin Stadium in Seville.

Real Betis' Nelson Deossa fired a ball at Bafode Diakite from close range after the Bournemouth defender fouled him on the wing.

Deossa's action resulted in the forward being shown a yellow card by the referee but Bournemouth players raced over to make their feelings known.

While most players jogged towards the incident, Real Betis winger Antony was seen sprinting to become involved and was seen pushing two Bournemouth players.

The Brazilian was then confronted by Scott, who was seen pushing Antony away and pointing at the winger.

‘Tangana’ en el Real Betis-Bournemouth que acaba con las expulsiones directas de Antony y Scott.



Surrealista. pic.twitter.com/yAsIWOzdAP — Gonzalo Tortosa (@GonzaloTortosa) August 8, 2026

Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Real Betis' Antony were sent off after a clash during their pre-season friendly

Former Man United winger Antony caused a confrontation between the two teams on the stroke of half-time

Scott was shown a red card for his involvement after he was seen pushing Antony away

Antony was then seen raising his arms and pushing Scott, with the Bournemouth midfielder moving away from the incident.

The referee ultimately opted to punish both Antony and Scott for the clash, with the pair shown red cards on the stroke of half-time.

The decision came despite Antony, who left Man United for Real Betis last summer, appearing to have been the main aggressor as tempers flared between the two sides.

Bournemouth had led the friendly 1-0 at the time, with new Cherries boss Marco Rose seeing his side go ahead through Marcus Tavernier in the 41st minute.

The teams exchanged quick-fire goals in the second half with Isco temporarily drawing the hosts level, before Evanilson restored Bournemouth's lead on the hour mark.

Real Betis equalised for the second time late on through former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals.

The match was Bournemouth's penultimate pre-season fixture ahead of the new season.

Bournemouth will face German opposition in Mainz next Saturday, before turning their attentions to their season opener against Man City on August 23.

Sports.title: Tottenham star Jan Paul van Hecke hits out at Getafe's dirty tactics - and claims Spaniards could have had THREE red cards - in fiery training ground friendly
Sports.content:
An angered Jan Paul van Hecke hit out at Getafe's dirty tactics after Tottenham's clash with the Spanish side descended into a bruising affair.

Getafe are renowned for their rough-house approach and showed little sign of abating during the 70-minute encounter, which was played behind closed doors at Tottenham's training ground and proved anything but a routine pre-season friendly.

In one instance, Sandro Tonali, who joined Tottenham for £100million this summer from Newcastle, was left incensed by a challenge from Mario Martin. After Tonali had beaten Martin to the ball and shoved him to the turf, the Spaniard retaliated by leaving a leg in when Tonali attempted to play the ball forward.

Tonali was left furious, chasing after his opponent and grabbing his shoulder to turn him around before pushing him multiple times, including once to the neck.

Several Getafe players rushed towards Tonali and the approaching referee, while Andy Robertson stepped in to shove Kiko Femenia away as he attempted to complain to the official.

Centre-back Van Hecke, who joined Spurs from Brighton in a £52m deal this summer, said: 'Sometimes it's good to have a physical game. I thought today was a bit too much. From their side, sometimes it's not necessary, especially in a friendly.

'I think in a normal game maybe they have two or three red cards. But that's also maybe the way they play. We knew beforehand they can do it.

'It's a friendly, so you think maybe they would do it a bit less. But on the other hand, we also need to be at our best because if you don't put your foot in, they're going to win it.

🎥 Sandro Tonali scuffle in pre-season 🇮🇹 pic.twitter.com/XTGblesDyj — The Spurs Watch (@TheSpursWatch) August 8, 2026

Tonali was left incensed by a challenge from Getafe's Mario Martin, rushing up behind him and shoving him several times, including once to the neck

Several Getafe players rushed towards Tonali and the approaching referee after the incident

'If that's what the game asks, then you need to put your foot in and battle with them, otherwise they win the battles. That's what you don't want. It's one of the first things you need to win in football.

'You saw at times it got a bit heated, but that's because of the reactions. If you get kicked, you're going to react.'

As for the match itself, the goals were reserved for the final few minutes worth of action.

Getafe took the lead in the 66th minute when Alberto Risco volleyed past Spurs goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky.

Spurs then responded moments later with Conor Gallagher's neat finish following a good run drawing the game in the final minute.

The home side came close to clinching the match late on, with Richarlison's header saved by Getafe goalkeeper David Soria.

Both sides had chances in a goalless first half with Lucas Bergvall's shot the best of the efforts for Spurs, while Andy Gray did well to block Ebrahima Drammeh's drive.

De Zerbi made no changes through the 70 minutes played with barely a break at half time, with lots of senior players involved in another training game played at the training ground on Saturday. Six young subs were named plus goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario. None were used.

Among those not involved against Getafe who are firmly back in the swing of preseason were Martin Dubravka, Kevin Danso, Micky van de Ven, Destiny Udogie, Rodrigo Bentancur, Pape Matar Sarr, Mateus Fernandes, James Maddison and Dominic Solanke.

Tottenham conclude their pre-season fixtures with a double header against Bundesliga side Hoffenheim next Saturday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium (3pm UK) and a Sunday match at the training ground (12pm).

They begin their Premier League campaign against Brentford on 22 August.

Sports.title: Newcastle suffer pre-season injury scare as Anthony Elanga is stretchered off following horror challenge from Valencia star - but new boss Matthias Jaissle receives positive update on winger
Sports.content:
Newcastle winger Anthony Elanga was stretchered off after a horror challenge that saw Valencia captain Jose Luis Gaya sent off during Saturday night’s friendly at the Mestalla Stadium.

The incident sparked a mass brawl after the home midfielder was given a straight red card for a high lunge that connected with Elanga’s shin just in front of the dugouts. The Swede was left writhing in agony on the turf while his team-mates emptied the bench and clashed with Valencia's players and staff.

Elanga received lengthy treatment to his right leg before a stretcher was called for, and he was clearly still in distress when he left the field. He had been Newcastle’s best player to that point and his loss was a sour end to the first half for new boss Matthias Jaissle, whose side trailed 1-0 at the interval.

However, the 24-year-old was able to walk in the dressing-room during half-time and it is thought he has avoided serious injury.

Sports.title: Confident Barcelona press on with Rodri swoop as LaLiga champions seek compromise with Man City over  £68m asking price for World Cup-winning captain
Sports.content:
Barcelona are confident they can reach a compromise agreement with Manchester City for £68 million-rated Rodri as they prepare a revised bid.

The Spanish champions yesterday agreed to send their captain, Ronald Araujo, to Liverpool on a season-long loan with an option to buy for £47m and are willing to offload a number of other players as they look to re-invest the funds into upgrading their squad.

Spain World Cup hero Ferran Torres is in talks to join Paris St Germain, while midfielder Marc Casado and winger Roony Bardghji were left out of the Barca squad that travelled to Udine in Italy yesterday for a pre-season tournament.

The 30-year-old Rodri has underlined to City that his desire is to join Barca and, while their initial £38m-plus-add-ons bid was dismissed as 'derisory', they are drafting an improved offer in an effort to bridge the gap in valuation.

Rodri originally had Real Madrid courting him, but they were 'respectfully informed' they were no longer his priority. His preference is to link up with Barcelona coach Hansi Flick at Camp Nou.

The 30-year-old Rodri has underlined to City that his desire is to join Barca and, while their initial £38m-plus-add-ons bid was dismissed as 'derisory', they are drafting an improved offer

Barca want to add a striker and a centre back as well, with Tottenham's Cristian Romero on their shortlist, among others.

Romero has been discussing moves to Inter Milan and Atletico Madrid, who are considered favourites for his signature, but a deal has still to be agreed with Spurs.

The 28-year-old Argentine will cost around £35 million and Atletico want to reach agreement before Barca attempt to step in.

Liverpool, meanwhile, expect Araujo to have a medical today ahead of completing the formalities on his season-long loan.

The 27-year-old Uruguay international is comfortable playing at centre back and right-back, which gives Liverpool coach Andoni Iraola vital cover as he waits for Conor Bradley, Joe Gomez and Giovanni Leoni to recover from injuries.

Liverpool are continuing discussions with Paris St Germain over a double deal for wingers Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.

Sports.title: Has Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler had ANOTHER hair transplant at 33? German shows off drastic new look just months after sporting a full head of hair
Sports.content:
Has Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler had ANOTHER hair transplant at 33? German shows off drastic new look just months after sporting a full head of hair

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler has prompted speculation he has undergone another hair transplant after surprising fans with a drastic new look in pre-season.

The 33-year-old was seen with a shaved head on the touchline as he took charge of the Seagulls friendly against Roma at the Amex Stadium on Saturday.

Hurzeler's new look was vastly different from the full head of hair he had when Brighton ended the Premier League season back in May against Manchester United.

The German coach had been seen with a shaved head during the summer's World Cup, having travelled to watch the tournament and work as a pundit.

Brighton fans have commented on Hurzeler's hair throughout their build-up to the new Premier League season, with supporters convinced he has undergone a hair transplant.

'Couldn't even focus on what the coach said, his head,' one fan responded to a post-match interview.

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler was seen with a shaved head on the touchline in their pre-season match with Roma, just months after sporting a full head of hair

Brighton fans have speculated during pre-season that Hurzeler has undergone a hair transplant

'I'm sorry Fab but your hair distracted me,' another wrote.

'He's previously been open about having had one [a transplant] done, maybe he needed a top,' a third said.

'He's had a previous hair transplant which probably didn't give him the density he wanted so had been using hair fibres to 'thicken' his hair up', another claimed.

Probably now decided to get another hair transplant

Hurzeler had previously suggested he had undergone a hair transplant after joking about comparisons between him and former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp during his first season at Brighton.

'In England I'm already being compared to Jurgen – which we can leave alone because he was much more successful and had a unique career,' Hurzeler told BILD in 2024.

'The only comparison that fits is that we both had our hair enhanced a bit.'

Hurzeler's hair had previously attracted the attention of Brighton fans after he was named as the club's manager back in 2024, with comparisons made to Jim Carrey's character in the film 'Dumb and Dumber'.

Hurzeler, who previously admitted to having 'enhanced' his hair, had previously seen his haircut scrutinised by fans after being appointed as Brighton boss back in 2024

Hurzeler will have been impressed with what he saw on the pitch as Brighton earned a 3-0 victory over Roma in their latest pre-season match.

Georginio Rutter opened the scoring for the Seagulls, with Yasin Ayari scoring either side of half-time.

New signings Luka Vuskovic, Costinha and Zadoc Yohanna were among those involved, but Brighton suffered a scare when Yankuba Minteh limped off injured.

'We took it quite seriously. I think also Roma took it quite seriously,' Hurzeler said.

'In their pressing, we could see that they had really analysed us and they tried to make it difficult for us.

'But overall, I think we brought a lot of energy and intensity on the pitch. We controlled the game with a good structure.

'In possession, we scored goals, we defended well, so overall it was a good performance.'

Sports.title: Revealed: Bruno Guimaraes reveals the 'no more fights' text he received from Declan Rice ahead of £75m Arsenal move
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes has revealed Declan Rice jokingly asked him to put an end to their on-field rivalry after completing his £75million move to Arsenal.

Guimaraes, 28, completed his transfer from Newcastle earlier today, with the midfielder set to partner Rice in the Premier League champions' midfield after signing a four-year deal, with the option of a further 12 months.

'Rice sent me a message: "Come here and please no more fights, now we're friends,"' Guimaraes said after completing his switch to the Emirates.

The pair have previously been on opposing sides of some fiery encounters, with Guimaraes and Rice involved in a number of physical battles during Arsenal's clashes with Newcastle.

In one such incident, during a Premier League clash in November 2023, referee Stuart Attwell had to pull the two players apart as they pushed and shoved each other in a moment sparked by Guimaraes smashing the ball at Kai Havertz.

Guimaraes is set to join a decorated midfield featuring the likes of Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Martin Odegaard, as well as Rice.

The pair have previously been on opposing sides of some fiery encounters, with Guimaraes and Rice involved in a number of physical battles during Arsenal's clashes with Newcastle

Guimaraes is also set to link up with three of his Brazilian team-mates in Gabriel, Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus, although Jesus could still leave this summer

The Brazilian continued: 'I was happy he messaged me, but the midfield we have here, in my point of view, is one of the best in Europe.

'Everyone is an amazing player, I'm so excited to start chatting and play, and know the players very, very well, but we have an amazing midfield.'

Guimaraes is also set to link up with three of his Brazilian team-mates in Gabriel, Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus, although Jesus could still leave this summer.

'Big Gabi was very excited,' Guimaraes added. 'Every time he sent me the message, "We’ll wait for you, when will you come?" I’m so excited to join them, not only the Brazilians.'

Guimaraes becomes Arsenal's fourth arrival of the transfer window after they made Piero Hincapie's loan move permanent and signed Christos Tzolis and Illan Meslier, taking their summer spend to around £145m as they look to build on last season's Premier League title and run to the Champions League final.

Hailing from Rio de Janeiro, Guimaraes joined Newcastle from Lyon in 2022 and was handed the captain's armband two years later. In 2025, Guimaraes helped Newcastle win their first major trophy in 70 years, leading the side to victory over Liverpool as they were crowned Carabao Cup champions.

His move is another complication for the club, who had already sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this window before Eddie Howe stepped down as manager on July 31.

Guimaraes described leaving Newcastle as 'one of the toughest decisions of my life' but admitted he felt he needed a new challenge.

In 2025, Guimaraes helped Newcastle win their first major trophy in 70 years, leading the side to victory over Liverpool as they were crowned Carabao Cup champions

'After playing two World Cups, I’m at the point of my life, I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I’m in the right place to do it,' he said.

Sporting director Andrea Berta added: 'We are delighted to welcome Bruno Guimaraes to our club.

'Bruno is a player with a great mentality and great quality, who will bring strong leadership to our squad.

'With Bruno joining us, we are further strengthening the heart of our team. As we have all seen, Bruno can play as a defensive midfielder and as a box-to-box player. He combines quality with quantity and has provided goals and assists for his team every year.

'Bruno will allow Mikel to further develop our playing style and will also increase our internal competitiveness, which is essential for maintaining the standards required when we are aiming to win major trophies.'

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
