World.title: Nigeria’s 2027 Election Will Be Fought in the Age of AI. Is the Country Ready?
World.content:
Artificial intelligence is changing how we work, learn, play, think and relate to one another. It is already transforming medicine, education, scientific discovery and economic productivity. Used well, AI could expand human capability on a scale few technologies in history have achieved.

But the same technology can also deepen inequality, industrialise misinformation, amplify political division and make it increasingly difficult to distinguish authentic human communication from synthetic persuasion. They can help citizens understand their world or manipulate what citizens believe about it. The defining question, therefore, is what kind of societies will AI help us build?

For Nigeria, that question is becoming urgent. Presidential and National Assembly campaigns officially begin on 19 August. Nigerians will vote on 16 January 2027, followed by governorship and State Assembly elections on 6 February. But much of the political contest will take place long before Nigerians enter polling stations. It will unfold on X, Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and WhatsApp; through viral videos, memes, influencers, anonymous accounts and, increasingly, AI-generated content.

Democracy has vital signs

We tend to measure democracy through institutions: elections, constitutions, courts, political parties and legislatures. These matter enormously. But democracy also lives or dies in the quality of public discourse or the everyday encounters between citizens.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Do we still recognise the humanity of people with whom we disagree? Can political opponents argue without treating one another as enemies? Do citizens believe democratic institutions can respond to them? Do people feel capable of acting together to improve their communities? And what happens when distrust, humiliation, ethnic hostility or political hopelessness become dominant features of the public conversation?

These questions led us at the Global Centre for Rehumanising Democracy to develop the Democracy Discourse Index (DDI). Built with a growing consortium of universities, the DDI uses a combination of human research and artificial intelligence to examine the democratic quality of public discourse. We see it as taking the vital signs of the democratic public sphere. The system analyses large volumes of publicly available discourse against indicators organised around four empathy, civility, trust language and democratic agency.

This matters because dangerous political environments rarely emerge overnight. Before communities become enemies, people learn to describe one another as enemies and before citizens abandon democratic institutions, distrust and hopelessness become normalised. We have seen this pattern consistently in our studies in Rwanda, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Eastern Europe. If we can detect those shifts early enough, democratic societies have a better chance of responding.

There is another dimension to the DDI that we believe is particularly important for Nigeria. One of the most consequential questions facing every society is how we prepare young people to live responsibly in an AI-saturated world. Youth must have the knowledge, digital skills and ethical framework to use these technologies to better their societies. Education must go beyond digital literacy. Students should be trained on how to use AI to evaluate information and to engage with and improve their communities and countries.

Teaching students merely how to prompt ChatGPT will not be enough. They need critical thinking to understand bias, misinformation and algorithmic amplification and an ethical framework for deciding what technology ought to be used for.

For the past year, we have been conducting an unusual experiment with university students and faculty. Students and academics in Pakistan, Albania, Greece, Bulgaria, North Macedonia and the United States have been studying public discourse in their own societies. We are expanding to Ecuador, Lebanon, the United Kingdom, Ukraine and Nigeria.

Students do not simply consume AI. They help build and interrogate it. They examine real public conversations and learn to identify empathy, civility, trust, democratic agency and other characteristics of political communication. Their human annotations are then used to train AI systems capable of conducting similar analysis at much greater scale. This reverses an increasingly common relationship between young people and artificial intelligence.

Instead of technology merely learning how to capture their attention, young people are teaching technology how to recognise the conditions necessary for healthier human societies. That is the kind of AI education Africa should be pioneering.

Nigeria needs this capacity before 2027

The implications for the coming election are substantial. Imagine being able to detect that dehumanising rhetoric against an ethnic or religious community is accelerating in a particular part of the country before it spills into offline violence; or journalists being able to distinguish an isolated offensive post from a rapidly expanding pattern of coordinated hostility.

And imagine being able to identify communities where Nigerians are responding to political disagreement with empathy, restraint and civic solidarity and learning from them. The DDI is designed to help make those patterns visible.

Fact-checking remains essential, but identifying whether a claim is true or false addresses only part of the problem. A technically accurate statement can still be used to dehumanise. A political conversation containing no demonstrably false information can nevertheless become dangerously hostile. And societies can experience profound democratic deterioration through cynicism, distrust and political helplessness without a single viral “fake news” story causing it. We need to understand the condition of the conversation itself.

Can Africa help build artificial intelligence that strengthens human dignity, democratic agency and social cohesion?

Nigeria should be at the centre of that conversation. Its extraordinary linguistic, religious, ethnic and cultural diversity makes democratic coexistence difficult, but it also makes Nigeria one of the world’s most important laboratories for understanding how human beings negotiate difference. That knowledge and experience has global value.

On Monday, students and faculty participating in the Democracy Discourse Index consortium will meet in a global virtual forum to present what they have learned from applying this approach in different societies. The event is free and open to participants interested in exploring how universities can use AI not simply to improve productivity, but to strengthen democratic citizenship and build better futures for their societies.

As Nigeria enters its first general election of the generative-AI age, we should aim to build the intellectual, technological , ethical and civic capacity to recognise and strengthen what can hold our societies together.

Dr. Margee Ensign is Board Chair of the Global Centre for Rehumanising Democracy (GCRD). She has more than 15 years of experience as a university president across the United States, Eastern Europe and Africa, including serving as President of the American University of Nigeria.

Dr. Jacob Udo-Udo Jacob is the Founding Executive Director of GCRD. A scholar of communication and democratic governance, he has held several academic leadership positions, including serving as Dean of Graduate School and Research at the American University of Nigeria.

World.title: PT Health Watch: What new mothers should know about postpartum care before leaving hospital
World.content:
Postpartum recovery is often overshadowed by labour and childbirth, yet the period immediately after delivery is critical to the health and survival of both mother and baby.

According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), the first six weeks after childbirth are a critical period for the survival and wellbeing of both mothers and newborns, as well as for supporting the baby’s healthy development and the mother’s physical and mental recovery.

The WHO also recommends that women and newborns receive information, reassurance and support from health workers throughout the postnatal period.

Speaking with PT Health Watch, a retired midwife, Mary Augustine, said the weeks following childbirth are as important as labour and delivery in preventing complications and supporting the physical and mental wellbeing of mothers and their newborns.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She stressed the need for health workers to provide every new mother with practical guidance on caring for herself and her baby before discharge from the hospital.

Essential care before discharge

Mrs Augustine said mothers should be taught how to breastfeed correctly, noting that proper positioning and attachment are important for effective feeding.

She also stressed the importance of proper umbilical cord care, explaining that keeping the cord clean and dry can help prevent infections.

According to her, mothers should also be taught how to bathe their babies safely, recognise when nappies need to be changed and keep the newborn’s airway clear to reduce the risk of breathing difficulties.

She said these basic care practices are essential for protecting newborns from preventable illnesses and discomfort.

Preventable complications

Mrs Augustine noted that many women remain silent about the challenges they face after childbirth because they believe such experiences are normal.

She explained that untreated breast pain, for instance, may discourage mothers from breastfeeding, while other complications can develop within weeks after delivery if they do not receive timely care.

These include postpartum haemorrhage, puerperal sepsis, hypertension, anaemia, abdominal pain and postpartum psychosis.

She also drew attention to perineal wound dehiscence, a condition in which an episiotomy wound reopens after childbirth instead of healing properly.

The condition may present with symptoms such as persistent pain, pus, foul smelling discharge, unexpected bleeding or difficulty controlling gas or stool when deeper muscles are affected.

“If a woman is bleeding, she can give up. We see them coming back emaciated and unkempt because there is no follow up. Sometimes their bodies smell and infection sets in,” Mrs Augustine said.

She urged mothers to attend postnatal clinics even when they feel healthy.

Why postnatal follow up matters

Mrs Augustine said the postpartum period requires continuous medical attention because serious complications can develop after a mother has been discharged from the hospital.

According to her, postnatal follow up helps health workers detect and manage excessive bleeding, infections, poor nutrition, high blood pressure and postpartum depression before they become life threatening.

She added that strengthening postpartum care and ensuring mothers receive adequate education before discharge would improve maternal and newborn health outcomes.

“Postpartum care should be treated with the same urgency as labour and delivery,” she said.

World.title: Kano spends N1.5bn on mass wedding
World.content:
Gov. Abba Yusuf

Gov. Abba Kabir-Yusuf of Kano State says the state government has expended N1.5 billion on mass wedding programme, covering medical screening, dowry, furniture, and other items for the couples.

Gov. Yusuf made the disclosure on Saturday during a reception and the distribution of furniture, among other items, to the couples at the Kano State Government House.

He said the present administration had committed over N1.5 billion to ensure the successful implementation of the programme and to provide comprehensive support to the newly married couples.

“This expenditure covered medical screening for all the brides and grooms to safeguard their health and that of their future children.

“Similarly, we provided the payment of N100,000 as dowry, in addition to another N100,000 as capital grant to serve as seed capital for starting a business and promoting self-reliance.

“We also provided household furniture and essential items, including beds, mattresses, and other necessities to enable the couples to begin their married lives comfortably.

“Government has also provided food items and other essential commodities to cushion the hardship they may encounter during the early days of their marriage,” he said.

The governor called on the new couples to strive to maintain peace, harmony, mutual respect, and understanding in their homes.

He reminded the couples that marriage “is an act of worship”, while urging them to conduct their matrimonial lives in accordance with the teachings of the Holy Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (SAW).

Kabir-Yusuf said the mass wedding programme, known as Auren Gata, was one of the key campaign promises he made ahead of the 2023 general election.

“Let me remind us that the Auren Gata programme was one of the key promises that we made during our campaign across all the 44 local government areas of Kano state ahead of the 2023 general elections.

“Today, we have continued to fulfil that promise. Before this wedding ceremony, all prospective couples underwent a comprehensive screening process.

“This included medical examinations to ascertain their health status, marriage counselling by qualified professionals, and participation in workshops and seminars designed by the Kano State Hisbah Board to prepare them for the responsibilities of married life,” he revealed.

The governor seized the opportunity to congratulate the new couples as they begin a new chapter in their lives together.

“As you were repeatedly advised during the counselling sessions, I urge you to be patient with one another, to uphold justice and fairness in your homes, to respect one another, and to live together in peace, harmony, and mutual understanding,” he prayed.

The Chairman of the Northwest Governors’ Forum and Governor of Katsina State, Umar Dikko-Radda, commended Gov. Yusuf for the initiative, describing it as a programme aimed at improving the welfare and living conditions of the people of the state.

Earlier, a prominent Islamic Cleric, Sheikh Abdullahi Bala-Lau, represented by Sheikh Kabir Gombe, said the initiative was capable of addressing insecurity and incessant protests spearheaded by idle youths.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that dignitaries present at the event included Gov. Umar Namadi of Jigawa and former governor of Kano State, Sen. Ibrahim Shekarau, among others.

(NAN)

World.title: ‘Patriotic leader’ – Defence minister hails APC National Chairman at 58
World.content:
Yilwatda

By Kingsley Omonobi

Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (retd), has extended his heartfelt congratulations and warmest best wishes to the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, on the momentous occasion of his 58th birthday.

In a congratulatory message, General Musa described Professor Yilwatda as a distinguished scholar, visionary administrator, and dedicated statesman whose commitment to democratic governance and national progress remains exemplary.

A statement by Leah Katung-Babatunde, Special Assistant (Media) to the Minister, made this known in Abuja on Saturday.

The Minister said, “On behalf of the leadership of the Ministry of Defence and the Armed Forces of Nigeria, I celebrate an exceptional patriotic leader, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, as he marks his 58th birthday. His insightful leadership, integrity, and selfless service to our nation continue to inspire confidence and unity.”

General Musa noted that Professor Yilwatda’s leadership at the helm of the ruling party plays a vital role in fostering political stability and institutional harmony, which are critical pillars for strengthening national security and sustainable development.

The Minister prayed that Almighty God continues to bless the APC National Chairman with sound health, divine wisdom, courage, and long life to serve the party, the nation, and humanity for many more years.

World.title: Troops disrupt terrorist logistics, neutralise IED threat, arrest suspects in Zamfara
World.content:
By Idris Salisu, Gusau

Troops of the Joint Task Force North West, Operation FANSAN YAMMA (JTF NW OPFY), have recorded fresh operational successes against terrorists in separate operations across Zamfara State.

The operations were conducted on August 7, 2026, according to a statement by the Media Information Officer, Joint Task Force (North West), Operation FANSAN YAMMA, Lt. Col. Aliyu Danja.

Danja said the operations disrupted terrorist movements, intercepted an alleged logistics supplier, recovered military-related items and neutralised an Improvised Explosive Device (IED) along a major road.

He said troops of Sector 2, working with a Police Explosive Ordnance Disposal team, responded to a report of a suspected IED near Jabanda village in Zurmi Local Government Area.

According to him, the team located and cleared the device, scanned the road and declared it safe before reopening it to motorists.

Danja said that on their return from the operation, the troops encountered suspected terrorists at Birnin Tsaba village in Birnin Magaji Local Government Area.

He said the troops engaged the group, forcing the suspects to withdraw into the bush.

A subsequent search of the area, he added, led to the recovery of two motorcycles, a camouflage jungle hat, a handheld radio and other items.

In Shinkafi Local Government Area, Danja said troops of Sector 2, working with the Mobile Police Squadron, acted on intelligence concerning suspected terrorist activity around Kwanar Jolof.

He said the troops engaged the suspected terrorists, who withdrew from the area.

A follow-up search, according to him, led to the recovery of a motorcycle, two camouflage uniforms, a camouflage vest and a jungle hat, among other items.

Danja further said troops on patrol near Maradun intercepted a suspected terrorist collaborator and logistics supplier identified as 35-year-old Lawali Dan Alo.

He said a search of the suspect’s bag, which he reportedly claimed contained food items, led to the recovery of N5.302 million in cash and a mobile phone.

“Preliminary interrogation showed the suspect was allegedly delivering the funds on behalf of a terrorist leader to another individual, Kasimu Garba, who was arrested at his residence. Both suspects are in custody for further investigation,” he said.

The Theatre Command commended the troops for what it described as their vigilance, courage and prompt response during the operations.

It said aggressive patrols, intelligence-led operations and targeted actions against terrorist networks would continue across the North-West region.

The command also urged members of the public to remain vigilant and provide timely and credible information to security agencies to support efforts to restore lasting peace in the region.

World.title: Tears, anger in Benue as 16 Otukpo attack victims buried
World.content:
Mourners weep uncontrollably as the victims are buried

By Peter Duru, Makurdi

Tears and anguish enveloped Efeyi community in Ugboju District of Otukpo Local Government Area, LGA, Benue State, on Saturday as residents conducted a mass burial for 16 persons allegedly killed by suspected armed herdsmen.

The victims were reportedly killed when the attackers invaded the community in the early hours of July 28, throwing residents into panic and forcing many to flee for safety.

According to residents, the assailants stormed Efeyi between 4am and 5am and opened fire on the community, killing 16 persons in what residents described as a brutal and unprovoked attack.

The incident has heightened concerns over the security situation in the area, coming barely months after another deadly attack that claimed several lives in communities within the same district.

At the mass burial, family members, community leaders, traditional rulers, political leaders and religious figures gathered to pay their final respects to the victims.

The solemn ceremony was marked by grief as mourners struggled to hold back tears while the remains of the deceased were brought to the burial ground.

A resident, Aboyi Owi, who attended the funeral, described the ceremony as one of the saddest moments in the history of the community.

He said, “The funeral was so touching. The atmosphere is full of sorrow, tears and anger because this was an avoidable death if those responsible for ensuring the security of lives and property were alive to their responsibilities.

“We do not know when our government will take genuine action to end the activities of armed herdsmen in this country. For as long as we allow armed herders to keep tormenting Nigerians, there will be no end to the mass killing of Nigerians by the criminal gangs. This is just the saddest day for the people of Efeyi community,” he added.

Prayers were offered for the repose of the souls of the deceased as mourners observed moments of silence in honour of those who lost their lives in the attack.

A Catholic priest led prayers at the ceremony before the coffins of the victims were lowered into the graves, amid wailing from bereaved relatives and sympathisers.

World.title: Infantino denies having affair, paying off ex-lover while at UEFA
World.content:
Infantino

FIFA president Gianni Infantino, who has endured a week of scathing criticism revolving around the now shelved private investment plan, has been accused by a British newspaper of paying off an alleged lover while at UEFA.

According to The Telegraph, the Italian-Swiss lawyer, who served as secretary general of European football’s governing body from 2009 to 2016, also previously used his influence to secure a promotion for the same UEFA employee with whom he was in an intimate relationship.

Infantino has categorically denied the allegations, according to the article which was published late on Friday.

When contacted by AFP on Saturday, a FIFA spokesperson had not responded.

According to The Telegraph, which did not cite its sources, this employee received a “a six-figure sum” upon her departure –- at an unspecified time –- in addition to the payment of tuition fees for a business school amounting to around £45,000 ($60,700).

When contacted by AFP, UEFA acknowledged that “a departure payment was made to the individual in question” at that time, “coupled with the payment of fees for an MBA course at a local business school”.

However, it insisted “the payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time”, before adding that “such regulations have been tightened since 2016”.

Quoted by The Telegraph, a FIFA spokesperson stated that Infantino, who has been married since 2001, “strongly denies these allegations”, which were “categorically untrue”.

“Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory,” FIFA added.

“No employee at UEFA and FIFA has ever raised a complaint regarding Infantino’s behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved.”

Infantino, who is standing for re-election next March, has been embroiled in a crisis since the announcement late last month of his controversial — and ultimately abandoned — plan to open up the World Cup to private investors.

He faces opposition in particular from UEFA, which on Thursday stood by its threat to boycott the World Cups, deeming the mere withdrawal of the controversial plan to be insufficient.

AFP

World.title: Real Warri Pikin cancels Warri show, rejects tribal, political divisions
World.content:
By Enitan Abdultawab

Comedian and actress Real Warri Pikin has announced the cancellation of her Warri show, citing “unfortunate divisions” in the state.

The entertainer made the announcement via her official Instagram account, expressing disappointment that division had emerged in a situation where she believed there should be unity.

“It is deeply disappointing that, at this stage in our society, we are still confronted with division where there should be unity,” she said.

Real Warri Pikin said the show, which was scheduled to hold in Warri in the coming weeks, had been cancelled because of circumstances arising from the divisions.

“It is therefore with a heavy heart that I announce the cancellation of my Warri show, which was scheduled to take place in a few weeks, due to circumstances arising from the unfortunate divisions currently at play,” she said.

However, she stressed that the cancellation would not change how she sees herself or the reach of her brand.

“But I need to make something very clear. The Real Warri Pikin brand is bigger than where I was born,” she said.

The comedian said she refused to be defined by her local government, the backgrounds of her parents or geographical boundaries.

“I am not limited by my local government. I am not defined only by where my father comes from or where my mother comes from.

“I represent every local government in Delta State. I represent Delta State. I represent Nigeria. I represent Africa. And as a woman, I represent women across tribes, races and borders,” she said.

Real Warri Pikin added that she would not allow her calling to be reduced to “geography, tribe or politics”, saying she remained committed to contributing positively to her state, country and continent.

“There are no limitations to what God has called me to do on this earth, and I will not allow anyone to reduce that calling to geography, tribe or politics,” she said.

She also thanked those who supported her during the controversy, including people who reached out, offered advice and encouraged her.

“To everyone who has stood by me, made calls, offered counsel, encouraged me and comforted me through this period, thank you. I do not take your support for granted,” she said.

While she expressed disappointment over the circumstances surrounding the cancellation, the entertainer said she held no bitterness towards those whose actions contributed to the situation.

“My prayer is simply that God gives us all the wisdom to understand that we achieve far more when we build together than when we divide ourselves,” she said.

Concluding her statement, Real Warri Pikin maintained that although the show would no longer hold, her broader vision remained unchanged.

“The show may be cancelled, but the vision is not.

“I am Real Warri Pikin. I am proudly Delta. I am proudly Nigerian. And I will continue to do what God has called me to do,” she said.

World.title: Ondo Rep member, Ojogo escapes death in Ore–Ondo auto crash
World.content:
By Dayo Johnson Akure

Hon. Donald Ojogo, member representing Ilaje/Ese-Odo Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, narrowly escaped death on Saturday when he was involved in an auto crash along the Ore–Ondo Road.

The accident reportedly occurred when a commercial bus made a dangerous overtaking maneuver, colliding with an oncoming vehicle and causing panic among road users.

Ojogo, who recently secured re-election to the National Assembly, was not seriously injured. However, some members of his entourage sustained injuries.

The lawmaker was said to be on his way to Arogbo in Ese-Odo Local Government Area for a political meeting when the incident occurred.

Speaking on the crash, Ojogo expressed gratitude to God for sparing his life and that of his team.

The lawmaker said ” God took perfect control of the situation and prevented what could have turned into a tragic incident,” he said.

He blamed the accident on reckless driving, accusing the commercial bus driver of impatience on the highway.

Those injured in the crash have been taken to a nearby hospital where they are receiving treatment.

World.title: Court takes charge of late billionaire Akindele’s estate amid Will dispute
World.content:
By Innocent Anaba

The Lagos State High Court has ordered the Lagos State Administrator-General to take over the interim administration of the estate of late billionaire industrialist, Chief Labode Akindele, amid a legal dispute over his Will.



Justice Tanimola Ajorin-Ajose made the order following an application by the deceased’s first son, Mr. Oladipo Akindele, who is challenging the validity of the Will and seeking to prevent the dissipation of his late father’s assets pending the determination of the substantive suit.



Akindele, who was the Parakoyi of Ibadan, died on June 29, 2020, at the age of 88 at his residence in Lagos.



The claimant had sued 16 defendants, comprising the deceased’s widows, children, relatives, associates and officials of the Lagos State High Court Probate Registry, over the disputed Will.



Among those joined as defendants are Rev. Michael Stephen, Prof. Wale Tomori, Rev. Canon Kolawole Jaiyeoba, Mrs. Oluwatoyin Isemede, Mrs. Abiola Aderibige, Mrs. Abiodun Duduyemi, Mrs. Ajoke Braithwaite, Mrs. Oluyemisi Oladapo, Mrs. Titilola Madedor, Mrs. Afolake Coker, Miss Ayodele Akindele, Mr. Mobolaji Akindele, Mrs. Mojisola Shonibare, Mrs. Roseline Akindele, Miss Samantha Stevenson, the Registrar of the Probate Registry and the Administrator-General of Lagos State.



In the substantive suit, the claimant is asking the court to declare the entire Will invalid, arguing that it failed to comply with the provisions of the applicable Wills Law and therefore could not constitute the legal basis for administering the deceased’s estate.



The claimant had also raised concerns over the management of the estate, which includes properties generating rental income, alleging that some rents had remained unpaid and that income from some of the properties had not been properly accounted for.



He argued that the absence of an effective executor or administrator placed the estate at risk of waste, dissipation or mismanagement while the dispute over the Will remained pending.



Ruling on the application, Justice Ajorin-Ajose appointed the Lagos State Administrator-General as interim administrator of the estate pending the hearing and determination of the substantive suit.



The judge ordered the interim administrator to operate under the immediate control and direction of the court and to file quarterly reports on the administration of the estate.



The court further directed all parties to cooperate with the Administrator-General to ensure the preservation of the estate.



The application had been opposed by some of the defendants, who challenged the claimant’s case and questioned the jurisdiction of the Lagos State High Court.



The defendants argued, among other things, that the properties allegedly forming part of the estate had not been sufficiently identified and that the claimant’s affidavit contained vague and speculative allegations.



They also questioned the territorial jurisdiction of the Lagos State High Court, particularly in relation to assets said to be located outside Lagos State and Nigeria.



However, the court rejected the objections, holding that the immediate issue before it was the preservation of the estate and prevention of waste pending the determination of the substantive dispute.

Justice Ajorin-Ajose held that it was not necessary, at the interim stage, to determine the precise properties constituting the estate before taking steps to protect the assets.



The judge also noted that the deceased’s Will was under challenge and that, at the time of the application, there was no executor or administrator effectively in place to manage the estate.



The court consequently held that the application for the appointment of an interim administrator was meritorious and ordered the Administrator-General to assume responsibility for the interim administration of the estate.



The order will remain in force pending the hearing and final determination of the substantive suit challenging the validity of the Will.

World.title: CDS Applauds Troops’ Commitment to Defending Nigeria
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General Olufemi Oluyede, has commended troops across all theatres of operation for their discipline, resilience and unwavering commitment to the defence of the nation.

Oluyede also praised the sustained collaboration between the Armed Forces, other security agencies, local security groups and relevant stakeholders.

According to a statement by the Director of Defence Media Operations, Major General Michael Onoja, the CDS said the synergy had continued to produce positive results in the ongoing campaign against terrorism, kidnapping and other forms of criminality.

The Defence Chief also commended the media for its professionalism and balanced reportage of military operations, urging members of the public to continue providing useful information to security forces to strengthen the nation’s security architecture.

He assured Nigerians of the Armed Forces’ unwavering resolve to sustain the current operational tempo until peace and stability are fully restored across all theatres of operation.

Major General Onoja revealed that troops of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai, had apprehended two suspected terrorist logistics suppliers in Monguno LGA of Borno State, recovering assorted foodstuffs and provisions allegedly destined for terrorists in Kukawa LGA of the state.

“Similarly, another terrorist logistics supplier was arrested at Gwalaram Village in Magumeri LGA on 4 August 2026. In a separate operation conducted on 3 August 2026, troops rescued Miss Blessing Tuggur, an 18-year-old victim who was abducted in November 2025 at the Dogoba Kopre axis in Askira-Uba LGA of Borno State.

“The victim was subsequently reunited with her family after receiving medical attention. On the same day, a suspect was arrested at Kan Lamba Village in Darazo LGA of Bauchi State for allegedly attempting to procure firearms. Similarly, a suspected terrorist informant was arrested at Dzangola Kilba in Hong LGA of Adamawa State on 5 August 2026,” the statement revealed.

The Director also stated that several family members of suspected terrorists had surrendered, while others were intercepted in Gwoza, Konduga and Bama LGAs of Borno State.

“Additionally, a group of 20 persons surrendered to troops at Kwuari in Konduga LGA of Borno State,” Onoja said.

World.title: Transcorp Hotels Launches New Padel Courts at Transcorp Hilton Abuja
World.content:
Transcorp Hotels Plc, the hospitality subsidiary of Transnational Corporation Plc, has launched new padel courts at Transcorp Hilton Abuja, adding one of the world’s fastest-growing sports to its evolving collection of experiences designed for guests, families, professionals and Abuja’s active social community.

The launch is the latest in a series of investments that continue to enhance guest experience at Transcorp Hilton Abuja, reflecting Transcorp Hotels’ commitment to creating vibrant spaces where business, leisure and lifestyle come together.

Speaking at the launch, the MD/CEO of Transcorp Hotels Plc, Uzoamaka Oshogwe, said: “People want more from hospitality today. They want places where they can work, unwind, stay active, and create meaningful memories all in one destination. That is what we are offering at Transcorp Hilton Abuja. Our new padel courts are another way we are bringing people together and creating experiences our guests will love.”

Regarded as one of the world’s fastest-growing sports, padel enhances Transcorp Hilton Abuja’s growing lifestyle and recreational offering, alongside its award-winning accommodation, exceptional dining, wellness facilities, swimming pools, tennis and squash courts.

Complementing these offerings is the Transcorp Centre, one of Africa’s largest purpose-built events and conference venues. With a 5,000-seat capacity and state-of-the-art soundproof partitioning system, the facility adapts seamlessly from intimate functions to large-scale gatherings, positioning Transcorp Hilton Abuja as a preferred venue for high-volume, high-level international conferences, corporate meetings, exhibitions, weddings and cultural events.

Together, these investments strengthen the hotel’s position as a destination where business meets leisure.

World.title: Oath-taking Video: APC’s Desperate Attempt To Smear Adeleke Will Not Save Him From Defeat, Says Imole Campaign Council
World.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

The Imole Campaign Council has described as laughable and defeatist the attempt by the Osun State All Progressives Congress (APC) Governorship Campaign Council to link Governor Ademola Adeleke to an alleged oath-taking video currently circulating on social media, stating emphatically that the governor has absolutely no connection whatsoever with any such activity.

In a statement issued yesterday by the Chairman, Media Committee, The Imole Campaign Council, Bamidele Salam, said the council is presently examining the authenticity, source and circumstances surrounding the video in question.

According to him, “It is important to state categorically that Governor Ademola Adeleke has neither authorised, participated in, directed nor endorsed the taking of any oath by anyone in relation to the August 15 governorship election or for any other political purpose.

“Governor Adeleke is a democrat who believes fundamentally in the freedom of citizens to make their political choices according to their conscience. He does not need oaths, threats, intimidation or any form of coercion to secure the support of the people of Osun State.”

He further said, “Indeed, the governor enjoys broad and demonstrable support across the state based on his record of performance and his personal connection with the people. His campaign is therefore anchored on his achievements, his vision for Osun and the confidence of the electorate, not on superstition, coercion or clandestine practices.

“The APC’s attempt to immediately attribute an unverified social media video to Governor Adeleke is therefore nothing but a hard-sell political manoeuvre by an opposition that is increasingly confronted with the reality of its rejection by the Osun electorate.

“The APC’s attempt to convert an unverified video into a campaign issue also exposes the poverty of its campaign strategy. Rather than engage Governor Adeleke’s administration on roads, healthcare, education, workers’ welfare, infrastructure, rural development and other measurable areas of governance, the opposition has resorted to allegations based on videos whose provenance remains unclear.

“But let there be no ambiguity: Governor Ademola Adeleke does not require anybody to swear an oath before supporting him. He does not require anyone to invoke a curse before voting for him. He does not require supernatural intervention to win an election. His strength is the people. His campaign is based on his record. His mandate belongs to the electorate.”

Salam noted that the APC should therefore stop looking for excuses in videos and begin preparing for the verdict of the Osun people on August 15.

“The people of Osun are not being asked to vote for Governor Adeleke because of any oath. They are being asked to vote for him because they have seen the difference between a government that works for the people and an opposition that has offered little beyond fear, propaganda and empty accusations.

“Governor Adeleke will face the people on August 15 with his record. Let the APC face the people with its own record.”

World.title: Benue ADC Guber Candidate Confident Atiku Will Win 2027 Presidential Election
World.content:
George Okoh in Makurdi

The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Benue State, Herman Hembe, has declared that the ADC’s presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, will win the 2027 election.

Hembe disclosed this in Makurdi yesterday while unveiling his deputy, John Abba.

He had constituted a committee to select the party deputy governorship candidate a few days after he emerged as the party’s gubernatorial candidate.

According to Hembe, the selection of deputy governorship candidate which has the endorsement of the national chairman of the party, Senator David Mark, was transparent.

Hembe said, “Let me congratulate Abba on his selection as deputy governorship candidate of the party. We constituted a team to consult and get the deputy governorship candidate and our leader, David Mark ensured the process was transparent.”

Speaking on the permutations, Hembe stated that all things are working in favour of the party presidential candidate.

“Our permutations are that the votes from the Southern part of the country will be shared between Peter Obi and Bola Tinubu and we are very sure that none of Obi and Tinubu will be able to defeat Atiku in the three geo political zones in the North,” Hembe said.

While charging the party members to go all out to work for all the party candidates at the presidential election, Hembe assured that there will be band wagon effects on the second election.

“Our hardest job is to work and ensure that our party wins the presidential and National Assembly elections, then, we will just go and sleep because that victory will have a positive effect on our election.”

Hembe promised that he is only going to spend a term in office to complete the eight years of Jechira Zone and create history to hand over to the Benue South senatorial district, known as Zone C.

World.title: 2027: Kogi East APC Stakeholders Back Tinubu, Ododo, Demand Power Rotation
World.content:
• Say East will no longer be appendage to any political bloc

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

Ahead of the 2027 general election, critical stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kogi East Senatorial District have declared their total support for the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo, while demanding a fresh and equitable framework for political power rotation in Kogi State.

The stakeholders, who spoke through a communiqué issued at the end of their Strategic Leadership Conference in Abuja and made available to THISDAY on Saturday, said Kogi East would no longer accept a political arrangement that relegated the senatorial district to the status of an appendage of another political bloc.

They also called for direct negotiations with political stakeholders from Kogi Central and Kogi West on what they described as “distinct, transparent and equitable” terms to establish a predictable framework for power transition and inclusive development in the state.

The stakeholders said their immediate priority was to ensure victory for the APC in the January/February 2027 general election, particularly the re-election of Tinubu and the victory of all APC candidates contesting National and State Assembly seats.

They further pledged to mobilise support for Governor Ododo’s re-election for a second term in the November 2027 governorship election.

According to them, the political objective was not merely to win elections but to reposition Kogi East within the mainstream of state and national politics and secure what they described as the “deserved share of development” for the district.

The communiqué noted that Kogi East had recorded the highest bloc vote for President Tinubu among the three senatorial districts of Kogi State in the 2023 presidential election, stressing that the district was prepared to increase its contribution to the APC in 2027.

He said: “We look forward to increasing our electoral contributions to the APC and to strengthening our collaboration with our fellow compatriots from Kogi Central and Kogi West Senatorial Districts to return power to Kogi East.

“However, we are resolved to mobilise total support for the incumbent governor, Alhaji Ahmed Usman Ododo, and his re-election for his second term come

2027.”

The declaration came against the backdrop of what the stakeholders described as more than a decade of political fractures, disaffection and missed opportunities in Kogi State following the 2015 governorship election and the death of the late former governor, Prince Abubakar Audu.

They said attempts to achieve political realignment in 2019 and 2023 were not sustained, leaving ordinary citizens of Kogi East to bear the consequences of prolonged political disagreements.

The stakeholders insisted that the time had come to heal the wounds, rebuild trust among the three senatorial districts and establish a new political understanding based on equity, inclusion and mutual respect.

They said: “We refuse to allow old wounds to permanently damage the deep historical linkages between the people of the various sections of Kogi State.

“Our only path to reawaken the political strength of Kogi East is to encourage healthy collaboration with the other sections of the state and negotiate truthfully for all that our people deserve.

“We reject any attempt to make Kogi East an appendage of any group in the state.”

The stakeholders invoked the political legacy of Prince Audu, saying his philosophy was anchored on statewide unity, inclusion, dialogue and equitable distribution of development.

They recalled that during Audu’s administration, major projects were conceived and executed across the three senatorial districts, including the establishment of the state university in Anyigba and the Obajana Cement Project, as well as roads and other civic infrastructure.

They argued that the late governor’s political philosophy should be revived as the foundation for a new era of cooperation in Kogi State.

“That is the true political philosophy we must revive today: vision, selflessness, courage, fraternity, equity and shared purpose,” the communiqué stated.

The stakeholders also demanded an immediate shift towards a predictable political transition arrangement, arguing that sustainable development could not be achieved where political succession remained a source of tension.

According to them, “We assemble here today to lay a solid foundation for Kogi East to be part of a realistic, predictable and harmonious political transition in Kogi State.

“We call for an immediate shift towards building consensus, renegotiating power transfer and rotation, and establishing an inclusive, development-driven agenda that guarantees equitable access to the instruments of power.”

The group also sought national recognition for Audu, describing him as a statesman whose contribution to Nigeria’s democratic development should not be confined to his final years in politics.

It urged the Kogi State Government to present Audu’s contributions to the Federal Government for a “highly merited and long-overdue national honour”.

The stakeholders cited the 10th anniversary commemorative events held in Lokoja in October 2025, which brought together national political leaders, traditional rulers and former governors, as evidence of the late governor’s enduring national stature.

They also noted the naming of a major boulevard in Lokoja after Audu by Governor Ododo and the unveiling of the Prince Abubakar Audu Leadership Foundation by the representative of President Tinubu at the anniversary events.

The stakeholders called for the foundation to operate as a nationwide, non-partisan platform for preserving Audu’s memory and promoting his leadership philosophy.

They argued that restricting his legacy to one election cycle or the final period of his political career would amount to historical injustice.

“Prince Audu belonged to multiple eras of Nigeria’s democratic development, from his early public service to his trailblazing leadership as the first and second civilian executive governor.

He must be remembered as a statesman,” they said.

In their resolutions, the stakeholders pledged to unify APC grassroots structures across the nine local government areas of Kogi East behind Tinubu and all APC legislative candidates in the 2027 elections.

They also committed themselves to dialogue with political leaders in Kogi Central and Kogi West, stressing that such engagement must be conducted on mutually acceptable and equitable terms.

The stakeholders further resolved to align with the state government to promote peace, inclusivity and accelerated development across Kogi East.

They called on party leaders, youth leaders, elders and other members of the late Audu’s political family to put past grievances aside and work towards a united political front.

“Our goal is to reintegrate Kogi East into the mainstream of politics in Kogi State and the nation on terms that will assure us of our deserved share of development,” they declared.

World.title: Idris Deserves Second Term, Says Zuru, Urges Voters To Support Gov For Continuity
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent

The Special Adviser to the Kebbi State Governor on Media Strategy and Communication, Abdullahi Zuru, has declared that Governor Nasir Idris has performed credibly well and deserves to be re-elected for a second term in 2027.

Zuru made the declaration yesterday while responding to questions from journalists who paid him a courtesy visit. He said the assessment was based on the governor’s record of delivery across key sectors since assuming office in 2023.

“Since the creation of Kebbi State, we have never had it this good,” Zuru said. “The governor has touched every sector and the impact is visible to the people.”

According to him, the Idris administration has prioritised the economy, infrastructural development, education, health, workers’ welfare, and human capital development. He noted that the interventions were designed to directly improve the lives of ordinary citizens.

On infrastructure, the media aide said the government has embarked on road projects, urban renewal, and rural development programmes aimed at opening up communities and boosting commerce across the 21 local government areas of the state.

“In education and health, we have seen massive investments in schools, primary healthcare centres, and the welfare of teachers and health workers,” he added. “Workers’ salaries are paid as and when due, and their welfare is receiving serious attention.”

Zuru further stated that the governor’s approach to governance has restored public confidence in government. He said the administration runs an open-door policy that allows citizens to feel the presence of government at all levels.

Calling on voters in the state, he urged them to rally behind the governor ahead of the next election. “I encourage the good people of Kebbi State to support Governor Nasir Idris and ensure he returns for a second term so that the good work can continue,” he said.

The Special Adviser also took a swipe at some politicians in the state, saying they lacked the pedigree to challenge the governor’s record.

“Some of them have held positions at state and federal levels before, yet they have no track record to show for it,” Zuru stated. “Leadership is about results, and the results are there for everyone to see.”

He noted that with the current momentum, Kebbi is on the path of sustainable development, and continuity under Governor Idris remains the best option for the people of the state.

World.title: Beyond Interest: The Alternative Bank Charts New Path for Wealth Creation
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Alternative Bank has concluded plans to chart a new course for capital allocation in Nigeria as it hosted investors, policymakers and business leaders in Lagos under the theme, ‘Beyond Interest: Capital, Innovation, and the Future of Wealth’.

The event focused on non-interest finance and the need to deploy patient capital into the country’s productive sectors rather than extractive models that only generate short-term gains.

Opening the forum, Muhtar Bakare, Chairman of The Alternative Bank, said the economy must move away from capital that merely harvests value.

“Extractive capital treats the economy chiefly as a place from which value is harvested. It may reward its owner, but it rarely leaves the economy stronger. Productive capital invests in enterprises, assets and systems that grow over time. It creates income for workers, demand for suppliers, revenue for governments and sustainable returns for investors,” Bakare stated.

Delivering the keynote on behalf of Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, the Commissioner for Finance, Abayomi Oluyomi, said government has a critical role in de-risking investment through infrastructure and credible policy.

He cited the Blue and Red Line rail projects as examples of public investment expanding markets and reducing business costs.

“The future of finance will belong to capital that is more purposeful, innovative and closely connected to productive economic activity.

“The future of development finance will increasingly draw on instruments including green bonds, sukuk and other ethical and non-interest structures that connect capital to real assets, productive activity and measurable outcomes. Investors do not invest in government promises. They invest in credible systems,” he said.

Also speaking, former Lagos State Governor and former Minister of Works and Housing, Babatunde Raji Fashola, urged financial institutions to prioritise investments tied to tangible assets and community well-being over those chasing immediate profits, noting that such investments deliver more lasting social and economic returns.

The forum featured expert briefings from Abubakar Suleiman, Board Member of Sterling Financial Holdings and a promoter of non-interest banking in Nigeria; Dr. Stanley Jacob, Group Chief, Innovation and Technology at Meristem; and Ajibola Tobi-Osho, Executive Director of Tugrande Alliance Limited.

Their presentations covered the business case for ethical capital, the potential of pan-African payment systems and asset tokenisation, and Nigeria’s macroeconomic outlook.

The discussions reinforced The Alternative Bank’s position that building a resilient Nigerian economy requires shared-risk, non-interest financial structures that give investors confidence and ensure investments create cross-generational value.

The bank said it will continue to champion financial models that link capital directly to real assets and productive activity as part of its mandate to drive inclusive and sustainable wealth creation.

World.title: Abia Leadership Academy, Strategic Institution For Training Future Leaders, Says Gov
World.content:
Boniface Okoro in Umuahia

Abia State Governor, Dr. Alex Otti, says the Abia State Leadership Academy was established as a strategic institution where ethics, values, and practical leadership skills would be instilled in Abia youths.

He said the essence was to catch them young, adding “we are committed to getting it right with the younger generation. Otherwise, our wider development efforts will be in jeopardy.”

Governor Otti, represented by his Deputy, Engr. Ikechukwu Emetu, spoke while declaring open the 2026 Youth Leadership Bootcamp of the Abia State Leadership Academy. The batch has 1, 000 participants selected from 7, 000 applicants. The training holds every long vacation at Government College, Umuahia, since the Otti administration came to power.

The governor reaffirmed his commitment to developing young Abians as future leaders of the state and nation and charged the participants to learn with humility and participate actively in the programme.

“This year’s programme is particularly significant, with 1,000 participants selected from more than 7,000 applicants. That response tells us our young people are hungry for genuine transformation—and they trust this administration to deliver it.

“For 2026, we’ve partnered with the Enterprise Development Centre of Pan-Atlantic University—a global-standard institution with ties to the World Bank, Goldman Sachs, and MasterCard.

“To our young participants, your selection is only the beginning. I urge you to learn with humility, participate actively, build meaningful relationships and, most importantly, use what you learn to positively influence your schools, communities and State,” the Governor said.

Earlier, the facilitator of the programme and Chairman of Abia State Civil Service Commission, Pastor Mrs. Eno Jerry –Eze, represented by Rev. Mrs. Ifeoma Agu, said that the programme was an opportunity to for the youths to imbibe the ideals of civic responsibility and urged the participants to be determined to use the lessons of the bootcamp to better their lives as well as bring about the change they crave for.

Mrs. Jerry-Eze thanked the governor for placing the youths in the leadership map in Nigeria and for leaving a legacy that assures that the leadership he has introduced would be sustained.

Delivering a lecture on the theme of the training: ‘The Demands of Stewardship’, the Chief of Staff to the Governor, Pastor Caleb Ajagba, noted that the governor was investing in the lives of the teenagers and young leaders of the state through the academy.

Pastor Ajagba, while describing the initiative as a strategic investment in the future of the state and a lasting legacy that will shape the character, mindset and leadership capacity of generations yet unborn, disclosed that by intentionally preparing young people for responsible leadership, Governor Otti was laying a firm foundation for sustainable development and ensuring that the ideals of integrity, innovation and public service remain deeply rooted in Abia’s future.

He added that it was an honour for all those invited to share their perspectives in the noble vision of raising a generation of principled, disciplined and transformational leaders through the academy and applauded the exemplary life of vision, focus, sacrifice, discipline, competence, integrity of Governor Otti and assuring of the unwavering commitment of the Governor to good governance and purposeful leadership.

Also speaking on behalf of the Executive Director of the development partner – the Enterprise Development Centre (EDC), Pan-Athlantic University, Dr. Uche Egbuna, said the future of every society depends on the quality of leaders it intentionally develops, adding that leadership was about responsibility, integrity and service.

Dr. Egbuna stated that the boot camp was built on four key pillars: leadership and service, enterprise, impact and innovation, and encouraged participants to strive for meaningful impact by becoming problem-solvers and change-makers.

He described the partnership with the Abia State Leadership Academy as a shared commitment to developing ethical leaders, resilient entrepreneurs and innovative young people who will contribute to economic growth and social transformation.

President of Abia State Leadership Academy, Prof. Kenneth Kalu, disclosed that 7052 persons applied for the programme and about 1000 were qualified after the rigorous processes of selection.

Prof. Kalu enjoined the participants to remember that they were expected “to think, reflect and become” future leaders, emphasising that what was more important was not that they participated in the programme but what they become from the programme.

Responding on behalf of the participants, Chukwuemerie Obiorah and Treasure Ogbonna thanked the governor for the opportunity given them to become transformational leaders, assuring that they would not disappoint but make good use of the bootcamp to better citizens in the society.

The opening ceremony of the bootcamp being coordinated by the Programme Manager, Abia State Leadership Academy and Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Public Communication, Mr. Dodoh Okafor, was graced by Secretary to the State Government, Dr. Emmanuel Meribeole; Commissioner for Tertiary Education, Prof. Uche Emeh Uche; Principal Secretary and Chief Strategist Officer of the state, Mr. Chinenye Mba-Uzoukwu, among other government officials.

World.title: SA refugees share wild wish lists: Gaming consoles, make-up and smart TVs
World.content:
Several South African refugees have been criticised over their elaborate Amazon wish lists. Images via X/ Canva

A group of South African refugees living in the US has been criticised by social media users for their luxury listings featured on Amazon wish lists shared publicly.

The group of predominantly white Afrikaners left their country on the premise of “racial persecution”.

SOUTH AFRICAN REFUGEES’ WILD WISH LISTS

On social media, a growing number of South African refugees have shared their Amazon wish lists with the public. Many have claimed that support and friend groups have encouraged them to list their “needs” and “wants”.



While some have asked the public to assist with purchasing basic necessities to furnish their apartments and fill their grocery cupboards, others have appealed for higher-end purchases such as smart TVs, digital cameras, electric scooters, and barbecue grills costing thousands of dollars.

Spotted on the lists posted on X are also non-essential items like:

Rhode by Hailey Bieber lip gloss set

Ray-Ban Lenny Kravitz Aviator sunglasses

Pro-gaming consoles, keyboards and headsets

King-size beds

Professional make-up kit and brush set

Anti-ageing face creams

Christmas tree and decorations.

@BraaiTo I’ve just seen your Amazon wish list. You haven’t been in the USA for a week and instead of prioritising getting jobs, and assimilating, you’ve got this absolutely insane wish list. Where is the Afrikaner pride? Do you know it costs the US taxpayers $10 000 per person to… pic.twitter.com/Ab1GxWroUR  August 8, 2026

The refugees have revealed that many of their items have been generously purchased for them.

Their actions have been criticised by a handful of South Africans who’ve accused them of “grifting” their adoptive country.

@kimkullmann: “You haven’t been in the USA for a week, and instead of prioritising getting jobs and assimilating, you’ve got this absolutely insane wish list. Where is the Afrikaner pride? Do you know it costs the US taxpayers $10 000 per person to get the refugees to the US, and the first thing you do, is try and leech off kind US citizens for insane luxury items!”



@AmerikanerB: “Every second refugee post I’m seeing has a wish list. Not a good look. Starting to look like a grift”

@RobKhulumaJones: “This seems like a well-planned scam operation to many of us”

MORE SAFFAS FLY TO US

According to government data, close to 3 000 South African refugees flew to the US under the resettlement programme in July 2026



Since the inception of the programme last May, close to 9 000 predominantly white Afrikaners have taken up refugee status in the US.

In May 2026, President Donald Trump authorised another 10 000 places under the programme, taking the effective ceiling to 17 500 in the current fiscal year.

World.title: Major pipeline repair to leave parts of Durban with 48-hours of water cuts
World.content:
A planned pipeline shutdown will reduce bulk water supply to parts of Durban next week. Image: canva

Residents and businesses across parts of Durban have been warned to prepare for a planned reduction in bulk water supply next week as essential repairs are carried out on the Southern Aqueduct pipeline.

The reduction will begin at 08:00 on Wednesday, 12 August, and is expected to continue until 08:00 on Friday, 14 August.

The eThekwini Municipality’s Water Operations Department will shut down the existing 1 200mm pre-stressed concrete pipeline (PCP) on the Southern Aqueduct to allow contractors to carry out sectional repairs.



The work is being undertaken in preparation for the new Southern Aqueduct Pipeline Upgrade Project.

Another water supply pipeline will remain operational

The City said the shutdown will reduce bulk water supply through the Southern Aqueduct during the repair period.

However, the existing 1 200mm steel pipeline will remain operational and will continue supplying water to the western, central and southern regions of Durban.



The sectional repair work will take place at the intersection of Perth Road and Hi Wycombe Road in Westville.

The City will monitor reservoir storage levels throughout the shutdown. Depending on water demand and available reservoir levels, some reservoir outlets may be temporarily closed.

This is intended to preserve available water storage and reduce the time required for the system to recover once bulk water supply has been restored.



Which areas will be affected?

A number of Durban suburbs and communities in the central and southern regions, as well as parts of the Pinetown South system, could experience reduced water supply.

Central region

The affected central Durban areas include:

Northdene 1 & 2 Reservoirs: Farningham Ridge, Hillary, Malvern, Mount Vernon, Queensburgh, Queensmead Industrial and Shallcross.



Firwood Reservoir: Farningham Ridge, Malvern, Moseley Park, Mount Vernon, Nirvana Hills, Northdene and Queensburgh.

Ridley Park Reservoir: Coedmore, Farningham Ridge, Hillary, Malvern, Memorial Park, Mount Vernon, Queensburgh, Umbilo, Umhlathuzana and Umkhumbaan.

Chatsworth 4 Reservoir: Arena Park, Bulbul, Chatsworth Town Centre, Crossmoor, Enhlanzeni, Ezinyathini, Klaarwater, Kwamgaga, Montford, Moorton, Phumphele, Risecliff, Shallcross, Silverglen, Welbedagt East, Welbedagt West, Westcliff and Woodhurst.



Shallcross Reservoir: Buffels Bosch, Burlington Heights, Moseley Park, Queensburgh, Savannah Park and Shallcross.

Harinager: Shallcross.

Klaarwater: Crossmoor, Klaarwater, Moorton, Moseley Park, Phumphele, Savannah Park, Shallcross and St Wendolins Ridge.



Chatsworth 1 Reservoir: Bayview, Bulbul, Croftdene, Havenside, Kharwastan, Phumphele, Silverglen, Umhlathuzana, Westcliff and Woodhurst.

Chatsworth 2 Reservoir: Arena Park, Bayview, Chatsworth Town Centre, Havenside, Kharwastan, Malvern, Phumphele, Silverglen, Umhlathuzana, Westcliff as well as Woodhurst.

Chatsworth 3 Reservoir: Arena Park, Chatsworth Town Centre, Croftdene, Montford, Risecliff, Silverglen, Welbedagt West and Westcliff.



Westcliff: Bayview, Coedmore, Havenside, Phumphele, Umhlathuzana, Woodhurst, Woodlands as well as Yellowwood Park.

Southern region

Several areas supplied by the Umlazi, Ensimbini and Folweni reservoir systems are also affected.

Umlazi 1/1A Reservoir: Umlazi A, B, C, D, E, F, V, S and T Sections.



Umlazi 2 Reservoir: Umlazi M, L, J, K, H, R, Q, P, BB, CC, AA, F, G, W, C, D and N Sections.

Umlazi 3 Reservoir: Umlazi J, K and L Sections.

Umlazi 4 Reservoir: Umlazi X (Malukazi), Y and Z Sections.



Umlazi 5 Reservoir: Umlazi AA, BB as well as Z Sections.

Umlazi 6 Reservoir: Umlazi BB, CC and AA Sections.

Ensimbini 1 & 2: Ensimbini, Ntabankulu, Draaihoek, Mahlabathini, Mangamazini and Mkhazini.



Folweni 1 & 2 Reservoirs: Folweni A, B and C, Golokodo, Dodoza and Isiphingo Esincane.

Pinetown South system

The planned reduction will also affect parts of the Pinetown South system.

N-Pumpstation: Klaarwater, Phumphele, St Wendolins area, part of Nsizwaqkazi, Savannah Park Phase 1 and 2, as well as Wiltshire Factories.



Washington Heights (Reservoir P): Klaarwater, Nsizwaqkazi, Regency Park, Latana, Hlanganisa, Gwala Road and Sarjoo Road.

Intake Reservoir (Reservoir Q): Demat, Progress Road, Mawelewele area, Intake Road, Luganda, part of Nagina Township, Khoseleni area, Sthundu Hills, Dambuza, part of Bell Tower Road, part of Grasmere Road as well as Mpongo Road.

The City said it will continue monitoring the network and reservoir levels during the work, with the aim of restoring normal bulk water supply as quickly as possible once the repairs are completed.

World.title: DJ Warras murder: Killer reveals how much he was paid for hit
World.content:
DJ Warras’ killer admitted he was paid R25 000 to shoot and kill the radio personality. Joaquim Armando Pacula was sentenced to an effective 25 years in prison. Images: Instagram/Gagasi FM and X/National Prosecuting Authority

The man convicted of murdering radio personality Warrick “DJ Warras” Stock admitted that he shot and killed him in exchange for R25 000.

The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) revealed the payment after the Johannesburg High Court sentenced Joaquim Armando Pacula to an effective 25 years in prison.

Gauteng police have also revealed how an intelligence-driven investigation led officers to Pacula.



DJ Warras shot dead in Johannesburg

DJ Warras was fatally shot outside the Zambesi Building in the Johannesburg CBD on 16 December 2025.

Police launched an investigation into his murder.

Ten days later, officers arrested co-accused Victor Mthethowakhe Majola on 26 December 2025.

Investigators continued their search for Pacula.

Police eventually arrested him at the Primrose Squatter Camp on 30 January 2026.

According to SAPS, officers also recovered dreadlocks that Pacula allegedly wore during the crime.



NPA reveals R25 000 payment for DJ Warras murder

The NPA has now revealed more details about Pacula’s role in the murder.

As part of his plea and sentence agreement with the State, Pacula admitted that he shot and killed DJ Warras in exchange for R25 000.

Pacula pleaded guilty to murder, unlawful possession of a firearm, unlawful possession of ammunition and contravening the Immigration Act.

The Gauteng Division of the High Court in Johannesburg sentenced him on Friday, 7 August 2026.

The court sentenced Pacula to 25 years for murder and eight years for unlawful possession of a firearm.

He also received six months for unlawful possession of ammunition and 12 months for contravening the Immigration Act.

The court ordered the sentences to run concurrently. Pacula will therefore serve an effective 25 years in prison.

The NPA said the State reached the plea and sentence agreement after consulting DJ Warras’ family.

Co-accused remains behind bars

Majola remains in custody as the case against him continues.

His matter has been postponed to 17 August 2026 for the conclusion of the pre-trial conference.

According to SAPS, Pacula turned State witness during the court proceedings.

World.title: Big Blow! Orlando Pirates key player suffer injury against Durban City
World.content:
Orlando Pirates head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou has revealed that captain Nkosinathi Sibisi suffered an injury during his team’s 2-1 win over Durban City on Saturday afternoon at the Orlando Amstel Arena.

A late goal from Ghampani Lungu in extra-time sent the Buccaneers into the MTN8 semi-finals.

The win came at a price, with Sibisi substituted at half-time. The captain came off and was replaced by Mpho Chabatsane who played the rest of the match alongside Lebone Seema.



Speaking after the match, Ouaddou did not reveal the extent of Sibisi’s injury.

“Look, first of all we know that MTN8 cup matches are all the time difficult and I think it’s the magic of this competition, nobody will come here in Orlando Pirates and to give you the game,” the Orlando Pirates coach told SABC Sport after the match.

“So, of course we started the game like what we want, putting the tempo, having control, I think we could’ve killed the game earlier before, but we missed some important big chances and I had to make some changes at halftime because Sibisi was injured.”



Orlando Pirates into MTN8 semis but Sibisi injured

The Buccaneers dominated against Durban City especially after Brooklyn Poggenpoel was sent off in the first half. Despite creating all the chances, Orlandi Pirates only scored their second deep into extra-time.

“I think it created some imbalance in that area; we conceded a goal. But what I liked it’s the braveness, character, personality of my team.

“We believed until the end and went until the into extra-time. But I think we could’ve killed the game before because Pirates really dominated that game,” Ouaddou said



Orlando Pirates march into the semis and are favourites to win the trophy for the fifth successive time.

Will Sibisi be missed in the coming Pirates games?

World.title: St Stithians ‘murder-suicide’: GBV org points to ‘toxic masculinity, violence’
World.content:
An anti-gender-based violence (GBV) organisation has called on young men, particularly teenagers, to engage in dialogue about intimate partner violence, on the backdrop of the alleged murder-suicide involving St Stithian teens, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks and Ethan Coetzee.

The bodies of the rumoured couple were discovered at a Sabie lodge on Monday, 3 August.

According to a preliminary forensic report, 17-year-old Cameron is believed to have been strangled, while 19-year-old Ethan reportedly took his own life.



GBV ORG ON ST STITHIAN ‘MURDER-SUICIDE’

In a lengthy statement, Not In My Name anti-GBV activist Lesego Mahlangu addressed the deaths of St Stithian teens, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks and Ethan Coetzee.

Mahlangu pointed to police initial findings that the deaths were attributed to a murder-suicide, possibly as a result of a romantic relationship between the teens.

She said: “We are called to reflect more deeply on the nature of intimate partner and close relationships, which are often shaped by toxic masculinity and harmful patriarchal norms. These are social conditions that not only place women and partners at risk; they dehumanise men by discouraging vulnerability, emotional expression, and healthy ways of responding to conflict, rejection, and emotional distress.

“While women continue to bear the greatest burden of this violence, meaningful prevention requires us to engage men and boys intentionally. We must demand spaces where they are not only spoken to, but where they are encouraged to speak openly about masculinity, emotional well-being, accountability, and violence.

“Challenging toxic patriarchal structures is not simply about protecting women; it is equally about preventing young men from becoming both perpetrators and victims of the same destructive system.

The GBV org went on to claim that the St Stithians double tragedy was an example that “violence knows no racial boundaries”.



She continued: “As we mourn and stand in solidarity with the Waldeck-Cooks family, we also extend our sympathies to the Coetzee family, who are mourning the loss of a young man believed to have been caught in the same cycle of toxic masculinity and violence that continues to devastate families and communities across South Africa.”

‘DOMESTIC VIOLENCE IN TEEN RELATIONSHIPS’

Former DA MP Phumzile van Damme has shared similar sentiments about the St Stithian teens whose lives were cut short.

She shared in a tweet: “We need to start talking about domestic violence in teenage relationships. Too often, the conversation, campaigns and support services are framed around adult couples, when the same patterns can begin long before the age of 18.

“If we want to prevent domestic abuse rather than simply respond to it, we need to recognise it earlier, talk about it openly, and ensure young people know what healthy relationships look like.”

She added, “I know someone will say, ‘No dating before 18 for my kids’. My baby love, they’ll probably date anyway. The only difference is they’ll do it behind your back. And you’ll miss the opportunity to share your experience, spot red flags, and be the person they turn to when something doesn’t feel right.

“Far better to know who they’re dating, get a sense of the relationship yourself, and create an environment where they can talk to you openly without fear. You can’t prevent every tragedy. But where there’s an opportunity to reduce the risk, don’t bury your head in the sand. Teenagers will be teenagers. Our jobs as adults is to make sure they don’t have to navigate inevitable relationships alone.
